review_text: A very cool experiment in game design, From treads new ground in the most efficient way possible, reusing large numbers of Elden Ring assets and reconfiguring them into a completely new experience. A little bit like a roguelike, a little bit like a battle royale, Nightreign has you racing against the clock trying to become as powerful as possible across two days before the showdown with the Nightlord on the third day. Defeating the challenge requires you to figure out a route through the semi-randomized map on the fly, avoiding powerful enemies until you've leveled up, hunting down ruins holding weapons with the boss's weakness, deciding whether you're better off going to a mine to upgrade your weapon or going to a high level fight to hope a better weapon drops. Each playable character is similar to a build you might create for an Elden Ring playthrough, but with a set of unique skills and passives that suit that role -- The dedicated caster has an ability that lets her recover spellpower and concoct new spells based on elemental residue, the greatsword warrior has a grappling hook that lets him quickly move in and out of combat range, the hulking tank has an ability that lets him briefly ignore damage and create a massive counterattack. Each character feels very distinctive, much more so than an Elden Ring playthrough, and having to improvise with what you find gives an opportunity to experiment with weapons and spells you'd never touch on such a playthrough. It's not for everyone, the relentless pace can be difficult to get used to, but I think this experiment is a resounding success.

review_text: It's addictingly fun and one of my favorite games I can't put down. It takes the gameplay of Souls games and adds fluid movement to the combat and I find myself having trouble going back to play ER due to how slow it feels now. The gameplay loop is fun and there's plenty of variance in each run, despite there being only 2 maps (yes, the shifting earths are variants of the 1st map, but there's SO many locations across the Souls series they could pull from, as they've shown from the selection of bosses). It's much more fun playing multiplayer. My biggest criticism is easily the relic system. Yes, it's a great idea and it makes for some fun builds and even more varied gameplay, but there's only 2 ways of obtaining decent relics, aside from some decent story ones: 1) playing matches and obtaining relics based on how far you went/if you cleared the nightlord. 2) a gacha-like store. And after spending millions rolling in the store, I can personally tell you the drop rates for actual good rolls is abysmal. It's no wonder why double Balancers has been the meta since the DLC dropped; aside from it resulting in some insane damage numbers on certain characters, it alleviates the main issue of the game of not having good relics to build around. The build variety in this game through the relic system makes for a very fun experience and it's a shame that it's severely hindered by tying the system to pure RNG. Even so. I'll see you all in-game. Gotta protect the flock, y'know?

review_text: I'm going to leave this review for those who are like me who love Elden Ring, but might still be on the fence about Nightreign. This is nothing at all like Shadow of the Erdtree or Vanilla. It's more of a spinoff than a real souls game. Nightreign is a wonderful game for people who enjoy boss rushes/gauntlets, speedrunning, or practicing and refining a plan many times over to perfection. It is fine-tuned to be a dream game for people just like this. It can also be a good activity for people to play a quick pickup game with some friends, since one expedition takes roughly only half an hour, depending on how strong the team is. Nightreign is a hard pass for people who like exploration, world design, "play at your own pace", slow boss fights using inefficient meme builds, or dungeon style beat-em-up combat over bosses. You will be punished for doing any of this. Nightreign expects players to be on edge the moment they begin an expedition. You don't have time to read prompts, look at descriptions, test out weapons, or explore non-meta paths if you aren't already moving to another boss area. The fortnite circle closes incredibly fast and you need to be leveling and gearing up as fast as possible to stay ahead. If you fall behind, there is no catchup. You will be behind the rest of the expedition. Sites of grace automatically levels your character stats. You use sites of grace as checkpoints to run through, rather than as bonfires for resting. The gameplay loop is like this: Drop in, Run to the nearest basic enemy (rats or hollows), kill them, run to the nearest site of grace, spam the action key to level up, run to the nearest encampment or easy field boss, level up at a site of grace, repeat until day 3. Note that every other basic enemy should be outright ignored for the rest of the game. Fighting them is inefficient and spending too much time on them will cause you to fall behind. I'm honestly not sure why they're even included in the game. We all run past them 100% of the time because we have to. If you're thinking that must be some tryhard speedrunning optimization, its not. It's nearly mandatory to do it this way for every expedition. This game is all about boss fights. Clearing field bosses as fast as you possibly can so that you have better odds of beating the night lord boss. This is Nightreign in a nutshell. With all that being said, I will at least give them credit that I really enjoyed the inclusion of bosses from past souls games. There are tons of easter eggs and references to DS1 and even DS2. It's just such a shame that I really can't tell you much else about the game, because the game encourages you to run past everything and go to the next boss. I don't even remember the designs of a lot of areas in the map (like random events and shifting earth maps). But I can tell you where to pick up another flask at a church ruin, i guess. The negatives outweigh the positives for me.

review_text: I want to like it. The core of an enjoyable game is there. But this is the sweatiest Fromsoft entry ever made and every individual part of that sweatiness is bad on its own merits. - Random drop based relic power up system. Requires you to farm away hours of your life on a random drop system that is honestly abjectly terrible. Most relics are useless for any character. Plenty of buffs are situational at best and managing relics is absolute ♥♥♥ overall if they expect people to manage different relic setups and large numbers of relics. - Putting a challenging boss behind a 45 minute playthrough with no way to practice it only works for one type of player. If you dont have good reflexes and have to learn the boss rather than natively dodging attacks on your first try, this game is punishingly hard. - Doing most of most characters life bars in damage in a single hit is not hard. Its lazy. The damage scale in this game starts bad and gets worse. Dying with flasks left because you never got a chance to use them because a boss combo one or two shot you is an extremely common occurrence. review_text: It runs and plays like Elden Ring (literally) but in a form of a rogue-like spin-off. It is focused on faster gameplay and online co-op. Nightreign takes 95% of its of weapons, spells and enemy types from base Elden Ring so playing that game first allows you to adapt much faster as you'll know ahead how things work. You start each run (expedition) by picking one of 8 (10 with DLC) pre-made characters, there's solo, duo and 3 player party matchmaking options. Each of them takes you on a ~40 min expeditions where you have to survive 2 days and defeat a night lord at the end. Each expedition has semi-randomized gear drops, points of interest and dynamic events. Combat system is the same like in Elden Ring with addition of new faster sprint (that removes the need for mount) and ability to climb walls. Between the expeditions you collect murk (currency) that you can spend on obtaining new relics (passive bonuses) or outfits for the characters. The plot is as basic as it can be and serves mostly as a background for the gameplay loop. If you just want to play as one character and see the ending credits, the game should take you around 10-15 hours if you succeed most of your expeditions on first attempt. After you complete the story you'll unlock expeditions against stronger versions of most of the bosses as well as "endless night" mode where expeditions get progressively more difficult with each their but you also unlock new slots for build customisation and can find gear with new types of passives and modifiers. If you enjoy the core gameplay-loop, you can easily get hundreds of hours of content out of this game. I highly recommend it (but also I'm biased towards FROMSOFTWARE games) for people who like action-combat rogue-likes and those who want more of Elden Ring after completing it.

review_text: ELDEN RING NIGHTREIGN is an MMORPG roguelike designed for players who love leveling characters and adapting their strategies to dramatic environmental changes in every single run. The combat is intense, driven by various types of monsters, tight time limits and equipment variety Unlike traditional Souls games, you can’t rely on a specific loadout all the time because the RNG always forces you to change equipment which affects your playstyle. However, you can use gem slots obtained the shop or after finishing run to add new traits that benefit your build and make your runs much more consistent. While most of the monster return from previous Souls games, they have been adapted perfectly to the game’s mechanics. The community generally knows how to execute a solid run, so there is no need to worry about teammates. If you are new, they will pin the map, lead the way and share loot. Co-op is spectacular, especially with friends, but playing solo is a great option as well. The game scales the monster down specifically how they engage and allow you buy Grace which allows you to gain extra self-revives for each day. The story is excellent if you pay attention to the character quests, which reward you with skins, gems, and journal where the lore is told. There are dialogues and scenes to help you understand the world setting, Niightfarers, other elements that go beyond just rushing bosses. The soundtrack cannot be ignored. It is beautifully designed and fits the game’s theme in every aspect. For instance, the hype goes sky-high during the flights. System requirement aren’t very high. My five-year-old budget laptop still runs it fine, except for the “Baron” boss which directly attacks the CPU. The DLC is also worth it. It meets all my points above and offers more challenges. Even though it isn’t free like the Everdark bosses, the DLC is worth the price for the additional experience in the new underground Limvied and old Limvied. Overall, ELDEN RING NIGHTREIGN executes marvelously in all aspects and is worth your money and time.

review_text: This game has a weird enjoyment curve. First it's fun as you learn routes and bosses and optimize your runs. You get to see a lot of older fromsoft bosses and it can feel like a nostalgia victory lap. You get all the bosses down, all of them being some degree of fun. Then you start realizing how awful the relic drop system is. This is managed to a degree by boss relics which tend to be pretty decent, but to get the better ones you need to defeat everdark bosses, and these are a very mixed bag, with some of them being just straight up awful bosses (ED Libra, ED Augur). Not to mention the 45 minute run back to those bosses. You somehow put up with this and see all the content the game has to offer before venturing into the depths. The depths are the worst way of making content harder because it's purely a % adjustment. Enemies just hit harder and have more HP. No different movesets, and the reward pool has even more RNG built into it. It makes the feast or famine aspect way more proeminent, except the fact that when you lose, you lose the equivalent points of 2-3 wins, which just feels extremely punishing. To get the best experience out of this game, play it with friends, beat the normal bosses and some everdark ones, and then stop playing. Even at $40, the game feels a bit overpriced for that amount of content. Also, in typical fromsoft fashion, the game has more than a few bugs and clunkiness, which can end up costing you the run.

You can't play previously beaten levels to grind, all you can do is play one of three challenge "survive 60 seconds" maps over and over for a miniscule amount of xp and gems. Gear is progressive unlock except from chests bought with gems. 1600 gems for 10 pulls of the best chest, or 200 for one pull. 15 gems per Challenge victory. See the issue? You're awarded gold at B5, 200 diamonds at B10, and 2 epic chest keys at B15 - each stage. So if you fully clear 10 stages, boom-2k free diamonds. There's a seasonal "battlepass" you progress via daily and seasonal quests - it awards chest keys, gold, hero unlock progress, hero upgrade tokens, and diamonds. There's 6 pieces of gear across 5 sets, each piece/set gives dif buffs. DO NOT SPEND DIAMONDS on revives or pass skips. Always have the Collector set equipped. Buy the 2x battle speed for 1k diamonds. Play two seasons.

review_text: Great game for the price

There are 64 achievements worth 1,630 GS of which 22 are base game totaling 1,000 GS achievable within roughly 45min or so. The remaining 630 GS & 42 achievements are locked behind the 62 USD dlcs or 30 USD Complete Edition. The game suffers from being SUPER imprecise due to choosing a graphical floating brush averse to an actual pin-point cursor. You can use the base pallete or click on the pallete for a larger range. There's a fill/paint bucket, around 5 brushes, spray can, and eraser. The base game has 4 chapters with 3 pages each, totalling 12, and 2 full chapters: Jungle & Space, 6 pages each, totaling 12 together. There is also a free-draw whiteboard. The DLCs offer 29 additional pages per chapter type, so chapter 1 would have 90-120 pages IF you buy the DLC. I think with all DLC you get like 540 pages & some whiteboards. Overall, great for AH'ers and parents with younger kids but the coloring is unfulfilling, in my opinion.

This obscure series caters to the most niche of veteran horror fans, who desire punishing, rewarding gameplay and cryptic puzzles and story that have to be deciphered with heavy thought, with lite-ARG elements that push the envelope. If you are experienced in this genre and can overlook the edges of the games sometimes being rougher, they are an unforgettable experience. The Injection series is some of the most genuinely imaginative and stylish psychological horror I've seen, turning classic formulas into something truly it's own. Tabula Rasa shows the creator's gained experience, with new features added and use of MetaHumans tech for cinematics, delivering a content-filled finale fans will love, and newcomers will find more accessible.

Even if you dont believe in the supernatural, your imagination does. This is simply a "story" horror game it is not COD. You haveto be willing to think and observe, but once it all comes together, it's intensely immersive. Just get in there, don't worry about what the game expects u to do next, and just be you in that world. You'll figure it all out. The only downsides i've encountered, and the reason it's a 4 for the moment, is the lack of non-game options. It runs at 30 fps only (on X) with no performance mode or blur options for softening the frame flicker. You could normally counter this by speeding the R stick way up, but there's no aim specific sensitivity slider. Just the one. So you're kinda stuck optimizing for aiming. But if you're not an FPS snob or senstive to frame flick, none of this should stop u buying this game. It is a unique and intense experience with a game that assumes the best of you, rather than assuming you're a lazy, incurious moron, and i respect the hell outta that. Good hunting.

review_text: Knew it was indie. But felt that, given the demo and footage, this game at least had potential. It really is much better than the standards I'd set for it. It does just a little bit of everything; fishing, scavenging, blacksmithing/gear crafting, cooking, has a great variety of play-styles to toy with thanks to all the dual-wielding possibilities and weapon types. Music, atmosphere and art direction are all above-average. There are slow-mo kill animations, varying landscapes and enemy types. And on that note I want to mention there's a cool feature involving a sketch book that you can take out pretty much whenever, and draw a sketch of whatever is in front of you. Overall there's a fairly large amount of content as well. This is a game I'd so far put on the same level as Oblivion (for the first time playing it), in terms of "a really cool, new dark fantasy RPG I can actually sink my teeth into." It's not perfect; there is some jank here. But what a breath of fresh air.

They wont be skilled, and they have their own needs. Taxes suck, but not really. You have ample ability to make money by hunting, crafting, and prioritizing what your people do. Build 3 woodsheds, and 2 excavation sites. Build 10 houses and the worker areas. Know that this will skyrocket your taxes, which are due in the spring. When you notice how prices work, you notice that meat and simple crafted tools are easily produced and sell well. Also hunting bandits for coin and loot is not hard at all. You can change the difficulty and game options mid-play, which means you can turn off stamina, or get infinite carry weight. Really, if you set up your villagers well, you can sell firewood for a living, and slowly go from hunting to having a merchant empire. Clunky in a survival sandbox way, but fun and replayable too. GG

review_title: The Game is better than the reviews
review_text: TLDR: The game isn't really that bad. Okay, don't get me wrong the game has it's issues, but most of the low reviews are just about it not having wheel support, if that's what you're looking for I'd suggest just waiting till they fully support it. Aside from that, the only real issue is the AI, which has been improved recently- it's still not super great, but you're not getting rear ended every time you stop anymore. The other biggest complaint is about the rolling at pick-up/drop off spots and stop lights, truthfully, this can easily be avoided by enabling your parking break when at a pick-up/drop off and at stop lights you can just hold the break button down..like you do in real life, and your car will not roll. Ultimately, the game isn't top tier, but it's also not really as bad as some of the reviewers make it out to seem- of course there have been some updates since some of these reviews, if you're not super bother by no wheel support, i'd give the game a try you might enjoy it.

The gameplay is challenging at first but you're encouraged to farm materials, teardrops (skill points), and exp. So it doesn't take long to start crafting a propper deck. The story itself is an examination of grief. You play as a mother who chases after her deceased son accross the realm that rests between life and death. As someone who enjoys brewing janky themed decks in MTG arena, I think Death Howl is a playground for mechanical experimentation and synergy hunting. I look foreward to chipping away at it over the coming weeks.

It's usually a pain to collect xp while moving through the map in these games but thankfully a magnet spawns in each arena and I usually head to it when I have about 30 seconds left. review_title: This Is Why I Play Videogames
review_text: ROUTINE is the first game I've ever reviewed. I absolutely loved it. This is the first game in a very long time that not only held my interest from beginning to end, but also genuinely scared me. The retro world design, the tone and atmosphere were PERFECT. iC bots were great There were only a few things I wish were a little different. SPOILER I really enjoyed the designs of the Type 05s. I thought they were amazing and terrifying at the same time. They unfortunately were nowhere to be found in the second half of the game. They were however replaced by something much scarier. Some of the game's mechanics never came back either. In the second half, I never had to use the bullet projectile feature on the C.A.T. again. Same with the finger print puzzles. I still used the UV function a lot, but I enjoyed the idea of thinking outside the box to learn codes. Although there were parts of the game I wish were different, I still loved it. ROUTINE is a prime example of why I play videogames.

review_text: When people talk about video games being art, this is the sort of game they are referring to. Sleep Awake is dripping with unique style and oppressive horror atmosphere. The visuals, art direction, sound and music is among some of the best I have ever experienced in a video game. Unfortunately, as you might expect, this seems to come at the expense of the actual gameplay design, as it is mainly very simple stealth and puzzle solving, with very straightforward exploration. Still, the incredible aesthetics, worldbuilding and immersion more than make up for this shortcoming. It is more of an art horror experience, and less of a game, so have suitable expectations going in.

If you've ever wanted a realistic police sim where you play as an everyday patrol officer doing mundane things like writing tickets, towing cars, responding to traffic collisions, DUI checkpoints, and on occasion intervening in crimes like robbery or drug dealing, then this game is for you. Keep in mind, this is NOT L.A. Noire, a True Crime game, or any action-oriented cop game. This is an accurate procedural law enforcement game where you are assigned tasks during your shift and are held accountable for any and all mistakes. Also, keep in mind this is a low budget indie game, so don't expect AAA quality. There is nothing else like this on console right now, and I'm glad the devs released this game. The devs confirmed they will keep updating and adding new content as well.

review_text: I see why people that connected withe original would be upset, it takes away the grind and preparation of building a roster of heroes and replaces it with long runs following a single customizable party. Nothing ever feels like a total loss. Great roguelike, DLC is great too well worth getting.

review_text: Time played: 22 hours 38 minutes Console: Series X Price paid: Free Play Days Achievements: 26/26 TLDR; If you're a fan of drifting and/or japanese car culture, this is a must own. Wait for a sale. I started this game with pretty low expectations, but was quickly taught just how much love was poured into this title. Cars look, sound and feel great to drive. The world is interesting and beautiful. The story is engaging and interesting, with characters that I came to enjoy and wanted more of. (Please do a sequel!) On to the bad; Framerate is inconsistent even in performance mode. The world, though beautiful, is completely devoid of any life. Some objects around the map cannot be broken when driving through them while others can. This makes for a confusing experience. Lighting is inconsistent across the board. Driving in cockpit view is hard to see due to a "tint filter" on the windshield, making everything near impossible to see around midday/night. Wait for a sale!

review_title: An Absolute Must Buy For Any Initial D Fan!
review_text: This is basically the best Initial D game I have ever played. The only one that really captures the feel of the anime. The setting is very similar, it has the story explained in manga comics that have sound effects to go with them, and overall it just feels like a love letter to that franchise and setting. The graphics also strike an attractive art style that's somewhat anime inspired, sort of reminds me of the newer Persona games. The car selection is great, half are officially licensed, the other half are obvious and well represented, all Japanese modern classics. You have 3 competition classes, drift, grip racing, and drag racing, and they remind me of the better Need For Speed games. Physics are fun to play with, music totally hits the Initial D animes, overall I am very satisfied with what I got.

review_title: Legendary sequel to awesome sandbox game
review_text: If you like sandbox games, loved and/or played the original Goat Simulator, or both, then you need to play Goat Simulator 3. This sequel takes everything great with the original Goat Simulator and cranks it up to 100. The map is huge and way bigger than the maps from the first game. In fact, the entire map is one large island separated into different cities or areas. The game doesn't fall short of funny gags or references, and you're sure to find something that references another game or film. You can now also customize your goat with the Wardrobe, where you can pick different gear or goat/goat skins. And now, for the first time ever, Goat Simulator goes online with online multiplayer with 4-player co-op, and you can either mess about or participate in some of the special mini-games scattered around the map. Goat Simulator 3 is a vast improvement over its predecessor in various ways. Definitely get this if you're a Goat Simulator fan or like sandbox games. It's worth your time.

There are roguelike elements like choosing powerups mid batlle and a recharging super blast. As great as the audio is, it is 2.1 front channel stereo only with no surround or Atmos. Also there is no HDR and the neon explosions and particles would greatly benefit from a wider color gamut. No 120hz VRR but it maintains a solid 60hz even when the screen is filled with effects. Buy this game, your subwoofers will love you and your neighbors will hate you.

This game is good. As the title suggests, it is short (around 20 hours) and slightly difficult at times (some areas and bosses being challenging) with a color loot system like popular looter shooters. Thematically, this game is the kitchen sink of other top games: feels like a mix of Cyberpunk, Doom, Metro, Titanfall, Dead Space and so on... I was pleasantly surprised for 3GB and under $20. It also has a new game plus feature so you can carry all your gear and stats over when going for another ending (there are several endings tied to achievements). There is a skill tree to cater to your playstyle that you unlock halfway through the game. There are "totems" in the world that add some rogue-lite elements. Only complaints are the lack of descriptions in the stats menu (mostly related to gear), and the ending being abrupt without elaborating on your specific ending. It isn't an RPG, but does have a couple RPG elements. Refer to the title of this review...

The melee and gunplay feel weighty and significant, you can feel every pull of the trigger and sword swing. But this game has shortcomings. Like DC, the movement is floaty and imprecise and the controls seem off like they programmed in an extra frame of input lag. Like other small indie games, there is no support for HDR10, 120hz VRR or Dolby Vision or Atmos. The audio is mostly confined to the front stage with little surround but if you're a bass head, this game has deep tight punchy LFE that will test your subwoofers. Overall a decent game that I'm glad I didn't pay full price for. A solid B-.

Also, if you're looking for games from the "recharged" series, those aren't here, you still have to buy those seprate...

Going in, you should know that this is not just a collection of Atari games, it is a playable museum and piece of history. Many people will hit the "X" button to play the games collection, but they are missing out on the main product. The UI for the timelines is very well done, as are the interviews, restored pictures of history such as cabinet descriptions and art, and more. Digital Eclipse went above-and-beyond in showing how video games got their start and why they are still around today.

review_title: New high bar for retro collections
review_text: This is such a lovingly consructed piece of software. Somehow they made a collection of games where playing the actual games is frequently the least compelling part. It is both a documentary and a museum. The interviews are terrific and edited really well. There's 3D-rendered product boxes and high-res scans of arcade flyers, development planning documents, and even business cards. I have no personal nostalgia, much of this happened well before I was born, so this is covering a bit of a blind spot for me. What a fantastic way to learn about the origins of popular video games.

Interviews and history are great of how it all began and to play it in order as you go along is awesome. We've all had our share of ''old atari games'' with all the rereleases and such but with addition of some ''newer'' never before rereleased (Jag and Lynx,+) made the purchase of this collection worth it for me. Got a Jag at Kaybee toys back in 95 on the cheap! Had a nice collection, gathering it all back is too much $. This is a well-produced title, packed with nostalgia and some updated games. Many of the classic Atari games NEED a trackball or paddle (spinner) to be any fun to play. If the programmers enabled mouse / trackball support, then arcade sticks that have a trackball and spinner would work with it, and this would be a five-star product. But the programmers did NOT include such support, so games like TEMPEST are unplayable on this package.

So I bought this awhile back and it was a wonderful compilation but more importantly, it covered a lot of history that compilations don't do. There are great interviews and snippets covering the history. But I came back to this compilation recently and they revamped the user interface! It's fast, colorful, and better laid out! Very nice polish with nice background videos. Surprised they're still tweaking this title as it's been out for awhile.

review_title: A tight concept spread too broad
review_text: A cRPG with minimal (and I would argue, disingenuously framed) character choices, skills, and progression needs an impactful narrative, compelling story, and realized characters to justify its minimal roleplaying. The narrative could work, but the story (the written scene to scene narration and dialogue) is stretched too thinly. I see a world where this could have been a great 2 hour experience that is instead 10 hours, manufacturing game mechanics that are only executed perfunctory or are abandoned soon after introduction. I think the narrative (and especially the flat characters, player character included) is just not crafted well enough, and rather than tighten scope to polish its flaws to create a stronger story, the scope was widened in hopes those writing flaws are obfuscated by, to be blunt, dishonest time wasting and false gameplay promises. I wouldn't be this bothered if I didn't think there was potential for better work in the future.

review_title: Great entry point game to the 4X genre!
review_text: Normally, 4X strategy games aren't my jam. I'm incomprehensibly bad at them and I prefer games where I can control the action directly and immerse myself in the world or a character that I created. While I'm still bad at these games, AoW4 is so customizable and accessible that even someone who has zero idea what they're doing, like me, can play the game and have fun. The possibilities for creativity and roleplay/storytelling are unprecedented. Just as an example, I have made Voldemort leading the goblins and Sauron leading the orcs as direct competitors trying to take over Narnia. I've made countless D&D characters from my Tabaxi wild magic sorcerer to my dwarf gunlinger and my dragonborn druid. Every single aspect is customizable. Want to make an army of ratmen who ride velociraptors and have orc strength? You can! Want to make Elsa from Frozen leading the Hobbits on a conquest of Faerun? Knock yourself out! Want to make Alduin from Skyrim leading an army of Khajiit? Go for it!

review_text: A phenomenal 2d platformer that's very similar to the Donkey Kong Country games. The level design is on point, and there are so many secrets to find. The music is great too. The two different characters are fun to play as and have unique movesets. You can swap between characters on the fly while grounded and in specific animations. The character that you're playing also as has unique team-up abilities with the other character, but you don't have to use them that much to beat the game. Generally, Marbles is more beginner friendly, but Checkers has more powerful mobility options. The story is okay... nothing too special, but it's cute and gets the job done. Windswept doesn't pull many punches and is generally pretty difficult, so there's your warning. There are accessibility options, though, so less skilled players can still play this game. As of right now, though, the camera can pretty janky at times, and game crashes every once and a while, so maybe wait for a patch.

review_text: This game is epic, pure and simple. Aside from the main story, the side quests are brilliant. There are no "go here, fetch this and come back" style quests. Every single side quest has some kind of interesting storyline full of twists and turns. I enjoyed every minute of this game, and can't wait to play through it again once hardcore mode comes out, not to mention the DLCs they have planned. This is a must play if you want an RPG worth sinking 100 hours into.

Quick PSA on how to install a mod on this version no worries if you already bought it or use Game Pass. First, the mod folder wonâ€TMt be there until the game creates it. The best way I found to trigger that is by launching the game, go to the internal mod browser, and install one mod from there. After that, youâ€TMre free to grab mods from anywhere. The mod folder will be located at: \Users\(yourusername)\AppData\Local\Packages\GIANTSSoftware.FarmingSimulator25PC\LocalCache\Local\mods Not in the XboxGames folder. Note that the AppData folder is hidden by default in Windows. To make it visible, go to the top of File Explorer, click View, then hover over Show, and select Hidden items. Just drop .zip files into the mods folder, and the game will recognize them. Make sure to open the .zip file you downloaded sometimes it contains another .zip inside. Youâ€TMll want that inner one for it to work. Use an app like WinRAR to extract it directly into the mods folder.

Moments where (in a PvP game), nearly the entire map came together to kill the ARC enemies and extracted together. Not a single shot fired at the other teams. Embark did such a great job of making this such an accessible extraction shooter. Get this game.

review_title: Almost perfect. Update: NG+ added, and it's AWESOME!
review_text: Sure, there are some little AA jank issues, mostly having to do with human facial and body animations, and there are a few audio issues I hope they can fix with a patch, otherwise, these devs figured it out. They started from the end of the 1st sequel, and continued on from there. And it's pretty great. They actually kind of invented a new genre of FPS game here: things like ammo and cover are trivial when you're Alex Murphy! And that is ultimately who you ARE in this game, if you choose, because, for the 1st time I think, you actually get to explore the psychology of being RoboCop in a videogame! But the action never gets boring, new abilities keep things fresh, and the writing is sometimes sharply funny, and heartfelt when needed. I could've used more music during downtimes, of which there are many, but they are filled with great moments of being a beat cop serving the public trust, solving mysteries, filling cop quotas; decisions you make actually affecting the world down the road.

And I was not very nostalgic about the franchise but after playing this I bought the movies lol. Minor bugs and glitches that will hopefully be patched. We also need new game+ and a instant action mode!

review_text: The story and gameplay trump the first title. But there are features from the first game missing. You can't rest or skip time. The visual upgrades to armor are now gone. Also, the game has graphical issues. It suffers from pop in and out. Screen tears along the sides and bottom of the screen. It gets grainy the longer the play session and also has ghosting too. The story this go around is more thought provoking and grounded. The companions feel alive and interact not just with the world, but the story. Its clear they focused more on story telling this go around and I look forward to future updates. At the end of the day, this game is great. GOTY

review_text: If you liked OW1, you'll like this one. It starts off a bit slower and there seems to be less emphasis about your spaceship, but all in all it's more Outer Worlds. There's nothing done with this sequel that would make you change your opinion about the franchise one way or another. Some of the new features are interesting, like how the game detects you are skipping dialog a lot so it will offer you a feat in which you get bonuses to certain things at a cost of others. Another example is if you sneak a lot you might get a bonus to crouched speed at the expense of making more noise when you get up. The gadgets are also cool. I don't like the extra emphasis on the guns skill this time around, but it isn't a dealbreaker. The starting world is a little slow to get going, but the second world (not unlike Avowed) really starts hooking you. I'm not sure why they have such a hard time with this these days, but it is what it is. Enjoy!

game_name: Complete Edition - Avatar: Frontiers of Pandoraâ„¢
review_text: I've never played a game where I felt like the world was truly ALIVE like this! The sound design when you're exploring the forest is incredable. The graphics are stunning too! I've seen some people say they get lots of blur when running but I have performance mode on (with motion blur off) and it looks amazing. I've also had very very few frame drops, most of which have happened when loading up the game from the instant game response thing on Xbox. The only thing I wish was better is the gunplay, but I think they may have made it intentionally wonky because you're a Na'vi, so using the bows feels great but the gun play is sluggish. Overall I am really really enjoying this game FOR WHAT IT IS and I think many people fail to do that. It doesn't do anything groundbreaking that we've never seen before, but what it does SO WELL is make you FEEL like a real Na'vi warrior. So if you decide to get this game, try to go into it with an explorer mindset and less of an "FPS" mindset.

review_title: Stirring up some flavor with a mix of ingredients
review_text: *Fair warning: I backed this game on Kickstarter* The art is delightful, perfectly serving up an atmosphere and aesthetic further augmented by the music. I'm unsure if there is a term for the folksy, western-punk space vibe, but if you think of a lighter, less gritty Firefly, you're in the right kitchen. The gameplay has been super tasty to me thus far, and I can't quite decide if I like the exploration or the cooking more - which might sound like a bad thing for a game with "Chef" in the title, but far from it. While a bit slow to open up at first, I'm already impressed by the scope, and am eager to progress and discover more! On the down side, this game is clearly made for PC first. While the console port appears exceptionally well done, things like the Inventory (similar to games like Stardew Valley), and some lack of context sensitive commands are indicative of these roots. Not at all a deal-breaker, but your mileage may vary. Worth a try for fans of cozy, cooking, and more!

It feels, looks, and sounds incredible. I'm loving the soundtrack. It is not a polished as the Criterion games, but it was never promised to be. This is not 2008 and this is not a $60 AAA release. This is 2025 and Wreckreation is an incredibly ambitious indie game from a tiny team. I'm so glad it's out and I hope it will be a success. I fear that with this niche genre, no cross-platform multiplayer (which I never expected), and the dire state of global politics, success will be elusive, but the game is absolutely worth $40. This is what Three Fields Entertainment has been building towards since Dangerous Golf, and I'm so glad to finally have my hands on it. review_title: Inventory system really hurts this game
review_text: The game plays well now, but the inventory system completely holds this game back. You end up abandoning most loot, which makes exploring the map and locations unsatisfying. There is very little incentive to explore most locations, because it feels awful leaving the vast majority of loot behind. It completely holds this game back from being rated higher.

I love exploration so this game was perfect for me. There isn't a clear direct quest line so taking your time to explore the world is satisfying and rewarding. I played on Survival so combat was a bit challenging early on, but you're not meant to take on mobs that early in the game. Just save often, pick your battles, play stealthy, and don't be afraid to run away or run past enemies. They will not chase you far and will lose sight of you quickly. The inventory is EXTREMELY limited but but on top of using the pneumatic tubes, you can use almost anything for storage. BARD crates, metal detector caches, crates, backpacks, dead bodies (not enemies), etc. The story was interesting and after playing this game for 60 hours, I got every achievement, every ending, and pretty much did everything. I loved it and this game easily gets 5 stars from me.

review_title: Extremely bad start, but gets much better.
review_text: It was a mistake for the devs to give you so few options for survival at the start. You're meant to avoid and run from combat at the start which does not make for a fun time. Stealth starts out terrible because of loud stealth kills and enemies that give you almost no openings. Having to buy skill trees was also a dumb decision. Once you find some decent guns and have a nice stack of ammo it gets better. There is a much larger emphasis on survival than something like base Fallout. You are a weak and pathetic loser at the start, so focus on the main story, explore, avoid combat and look for recipes/trade items. You'll unlock cooler stuff later on. Only glitch I've had is the sound one(series X). You can have fun with the game, but you have to play a very specific way.

They took the story of Stalker, the gun fighting of Farcry, and the "survival" mechanic of Tomb Raider and it didn't work. They got the short comings of all of them with zero of the magic. Every single thing in this game was done 5x better else where. Not a single new idea. I played right up to the end finally i was just too bored. Every aspect gets old from the combat, the exploration, and the paper thin plot and characters. You will have more fun playing almost any other game.

The game is gorgeous and thats about all it has going for it. How are you meant to enjoy the scenery when the basic movement controls are floaty and inconsistent. I got mild motion sickness during combat. Trying to get your cursor over lootables is as awkward as trying to find them in the first place. It makes exploration, one of the game's 3 core aspects, completely unenjoyable. Frustratingly disappointed.

And if you lose, you get to start all over again from the very beginning. Yay. The first five or six days of play are a twenty minute long, absolute yawning snoozefest in which you do nothing except micromanage your incredibly limited workforce in order to grow your incredibly limited resources so that you can maybe survive to day twenty. review_text: Get your trigger fingers and reflexes ready for the undead have returned to wreak havoc in The House of the Dead 2. This remake brings back everything I missed from originally playing this on the Dreamcast along with some upgrades. This on rails arcade shooter runs smooth from start to finish. Sure the voice lines have been redone by different actors and some of the boss creature sounds have been tweaked but if you lower the nostalgia glasses a little bit, it's still the same campy dialogue and a blast to play since 98. Graphics and character models have been vastly improved with everything being more gritty and detailed. Achievements have been added and unlock even with cheats active. review_title: We Can Make It If We Run
review_text: Deep in the Brazilian jungle, a team of military police have been dispatched to investigate a series of animal attacks. This investigation quickly turns into a pre-historic nightmare they must survive. Acre Crisis is trying to scratch a dinosaur survival game itch we all have. With a graphic style from decades ago, limited ammo supply and a mysterious story, it has the right setup. Which it does execute well because I did like how the story and events are fleshed out. It's just what happened when it came to the controller layout? RT for aim and B to shoot was a terrible idea. However, if you can get past that, the only other real negative is getting stuck on everything. Thankfully there's a generous jump feature that overcomes getting caught on everything, especially when running from dinos. In the jungle, they're nonstop, you have to run. With easy achievements, good dino design, dino sounds and a decent story; I liked it. Mostly devs, improve upon the controls for the sequel please.

First of all, i have over 100 hours of playtime on PS5. This is a survival/roguelike with spooky atmosphere. This game has one of the coolest survival mechanics. Your car is what keeps you alive. its a mobile safe zone. Well... almost, you have to keep it up and running and the doors intact. Every part of the car adds to its ability to shield you from the hazards in the zone. You start with a simple station wagon and eventually beef it up to a mobile fortress. There are so many awesome upgrades you can customize your car with, spotlights, extra storage, decals and paint. Heck why not add a huge tank of gas to the roof? You can do this and much more, how you customize it is up to you. Your real safe area is the garage. it is where you return with all of the goodies you collected to create upgrades for your car and yourself. To make it even better, you can upgrade the garage too. review_title: Commitment and Patience Required; But Worth It
review_text: The game just released and focuses on building, crafting, and exploration. It takes a looong time to skill up, but that's the intent. This isn't a game with a 60-hour completion. It's something you continuously play and build community around. This game has just released 1.0 and has several continuous releases planned. If you're just starting, you have the opportunity to level up and build your home and marketplace or choose your own adventure before the expansions introduce battle. There are PVP and PVE areas. You are offered multiple weapon crafting choices from swords to spears to magic staffs. If you want to rule Pax Dei I'd recommend starting early and plan on investing a lot of time. Some other reviews don't understand the vision for the game and completely miss the mark. Again, this is a game about commitment and community; NOT a game that is meant to be finished over the course of a weekend.

The building system is fantastic, and is definitely the game's standout feature. I've run across many amazing builds, from cozy roadside inns to elaborate cities and castles. The game does need more content in terms of mob variety, things to do in the world, and a smoother new player experience.

review_title: You can play with a plot for free
review_text: I don't get the whole "hate this game cuz it's not free" - but I've been playing for 3 months, with a plot, and never had to pay. There is in-game currency called Grace. Logging in every day gets you grace, or killing NPCs earns you gold, which you can use to buy grace. If you play fairly regularly, you can play for free, including a plot. You can't build giant castles with one plot, but it's big enough to build a multi-story building with plenty of room. Game is beautiful. It IS very grindy. A lot to craft and build amazing looking buildings - takes a looong time to unlock the more interesting stuff. Relaxing for me, but may be too much grind for many people. The world is also huge, and while player buildings are everywhere, I'll see 4-5 people at most in a session. Either bring friends, make them, or plan solo. Community has been very friendly. The combat is pretty basic and repetitive, and the NPCs are fairly obtuse. For me, they are means to earning gold.

TL;dr - Old school shooter that is handled in a smart way so it holds up by modern standards too. It doesn't just depend on retro nostalgia like some other games I've played. Game itself is well thought out and shows the good side of classic FPS design. Open levels without waypoints and rewards for reaching difficult to find areas. It has some light switch/platforming puzzles with very meaty combat. All weapons have 2 modes that both feel useful through the entire game. Example: Basic pistol can shoot fast for beefy targets or use a limited lock-on to snipe distant targets or clear small groups (which is great to have on the basic gun, since scoped weapons aren't a thing here.) Just like a classic FPS, you will rely on manual saves but there are some autosaves if you're forgetful.

review_text: This game took me by surprise. Wanted to just try it out and ended up completing it A unique pinball roguelite. The only Roguelite I've completed 100% besides vampire survivors. Gets even better you can use more balls, passives and 2 characters for your runs. Highly recommended for those who like Roguelites, pinball or both. Even if you don't this is a chill game to play with Spotify in the background! Tip for base building. review_text: I agonized between 3 or 4 stars but settled on 3. I love the first two Little Nightmare games but found this one lacking. What I mean is, is you'll be in an area doing a puzzle and theres just rooms that serve no narrative purpose and arent really interesting they're just there. The first two games also crafted an interesting story with no dialogue and had interesting twists, this? I was never really engrossed in its story. Supposedly the devs are doing more story stuff through upcoming DLC but thats basically charging you to complete the story that the main game should have already done. The game does have highlights of course the Carnivale and Stage levels are highlights but the Desert and Hospital ones drag it down. This review hurt to write as I was genuinely pumped for Little Nightmares III but I was let down by it.

review_title: A for effort, C- for execution...
review_text: A Castlevania clone with the OG Dracula - sounds like a dream, and... Sadly it underdelivers, massively. The good: - It looks like Castlevania - Officially licensed by Bela Lugosi's estate The bad: - A bareboned experience, right from the starting menu that has two options - Play or Quit, and no settings - Vast and empty locations, paired with a small character sprite. I get the idea and the limitations, but it's sub-par - Sluggish controls. Yes, I get the Castlevania 1-3 blueprint, but at least add a Metroid-esque "stop to aim" button if you're letting us whip in 8 directions - Poor and straight up baffling level design. There's a difference between hard and deliberately unfair. This one falls into the latter category. And exploration is limited to tiny detours on mostly bite-size maps through breakable walls - There are hearts in almost every light source, like in Castlevania, but they're supposed to be health... Yet they barely heal. - Ridiculously easy bosses $5 tops

Just like old school Castlevania, except with less frustration if you die at a difficult room...and they dug up Bela Lugosi to represent Dracula, which is a long overdue tip of the hat to the OG greatest Drac of them all.

Caring for your beloved horse is not all that you do there are also things around the stable that need fixing so in order to do that you can enter competitions. These are just timing your jumping so you don't knock down bars. After awhile you are able to train your trusting steed to improve and enhance both of your abilities. I give this game five stars because it to me is the best game you can get if you just want to relax with horses.

review_title: Pretty good learning sim but also a reminder
review_text: Pretty decent learning sim for basic rules of the road, I do have a couple issues I'm not a fan of. Firstly rules are little too strict, if i turn on a blinker just a little too far back for the games liking it deducts points although in my opinion it's within reason to turn on a blinker that far back in some cases for other drivers. My second issue is the AI is relentless which is fine sometimes for learning but EVERY AI acts like you aren't even there and just pulls out in front of you. Also right of way doesn't exist in this game. Lastly a reminder that this teaches basic lessons, depending on where someone lives these lessons aren't helping completely. For example I'm in the USA in a smaller major city and most drivers ignore these rules, like everyone in my city regularly goes 10-20 over the limit and they really don't care if you are following the rules or not they will hit you. Again a good learning tool, but I wouldn't say this game will work for every situation.

review_text: I bought this expecting a lower budget, if decent Aliens game. Kinda a 'they tried really hard, even if it's just alright' thing. Something that most people would pass on, but Aliens fans would enjoy for the sake of it being Aliens. (Because to be honest with you, as an Aliens fan, I'd play just about any game that lets me hear that sweet, delectable Pulse Rifle noise.) But this actually turned out to be a surpisingly good horror-shooter. The voice acting and story are decent, the gameplay is smooth, the Xeno AI is really good, the Pulse Rifle sounds are indeed delectable, and I like the horror aspects- safe rooms, scarce resources, limited saves etc. Turned out to be a genuinely good game. You could enjoy this even if you aren't a big fan of the series, but there are plenty of references for big fans too. Just remember this is just PART ONE, so it isn't extremely long, (I don't think it's too short either though, imo) but there will be more. I can't wait for that.

But it really struggles on the Xbox - the hitboxes for items work less than half the time, so your character will fruitlessly ape watering, harvesting or picking something up, from multiple angles, over multiple attempts, before FINALLY achieving whatever simple task they're trying to do. As this is a farming sim, being unable to merely water and harvest your crops without each single movement requiring numerous tries is rather aggravating, to say the least. I've witnessed my character cycle through entering the same door I just left, over and over again, since the game automatically pushes you through any door you are near, regardless of whether or not you just exited it. My character also randomly creeps towards interactive objects, which I have to constantly correct. And all this happens while the game's clock is ticking. game_name: Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds Digital Deluxe Edition
review_text: I pre-ordered this game months before its release, as well as Sonic Frontiers and Sonic x Shadow generations. Sega has a knack for letting their projects slow burn, even in the midst of competitive sales from other gaming companies. Time and time again however, they have shown us that you dont need to keep up with trends to sell great games. Sega has also shown us that if it aint broke, don't fix it! Sonic Racing: Crossworlds is immersive from the moment you load the game! Awesome cut scenes, banger soundtracks (even tracks from older sonic games!), extensive customization of characters and vehicles (with more of both being released throughout the end of the year), and the RACETRACKS! The concept of switching to a new world is genius! The unpredictability and randomness only adds to the enjoyment. Even online crossplay is great! My friend and I were able to join up quickly after our first grand prix. Hopefully in the future they'll add voice chat? I had to stay on the phone with him.

I can see this game evolving into Dying Light 3 overtime the more Techland (hopefully) fixes and adds more to this game.

review_title: BEST CO-OP HORROR GAME ON XBOX!
review_text: This game is exactly what a horror game should be. This game is not full of cheap jumpscares and is actually immersive and random. The creatures don't just wait for you in one spot to jump out at you. They actually wander around the maps randomly. Each creature has completely different looks, behavior, weaknesses and strengths. Great soundtrack and the puzzles are insanely fun to figure out with friends because they aren't too hard or complicated, but still enough to make you think for 5 to 10 minutes. I haven't beat the story yet. Im playing with my older cousin we've always been close and play every night online. The story is very interesting and creepy, but not predictable. We have no idea what's going to happen next! Great Co-op game and scary but not too scary to handle. I recommend to everyone who has a friend or relative that they like to play with, as long as you can handle a little bit of scare! Also everyone who says online multiplayer doesn't work, it's definitely been fixed

review_text: It's really interesting - I didn't think a whole lot on the Hidden Cats series of games, besides generally all being easy and quick gamerscore. I've been on a light achievement hunting binge since late 2025, I figured stuff like this couldn't hurt. It began to feel a lot more depth-filled when I saw some of the care these devs gave not only to the setting, but the actual act of seeking out everything in a level. Not only does it go full 80's sci-fi anime type of zany, but the game's filled with special cards to signify locales, items, even IRL dev cats (all of which, yes, are cute). It's all very admirable to me. Don't get me wrong, the premise is still simple, and your time will inevitably be short with this one. But in a world full of VERY involved, complicated franchises... little ones like these? They're nice. Pick this up if you need a break between games. Can't hurt. Especially since proceeds get donated to animal shelters!

review_title: As a fan of the first game..
review_text: In short; It's cleaned up but watered down. First off, I really like the art direction of this game. It creates a colorful, comic like world. The game plays smooth and clean as well. It feels good. There is definitely fun to be had here. In fact, I can say the game is really starting to grow on me. However.. I really wish they would have kept the same weapons from the first game and just capitalized on them. I liked how some of the weapons from the first game were a bit different from other kart racers and gave you unique abilities that really played into the mechanics of the game. The weapons in this game are all basically just reskinned from Mario Kart. (No, I didn't buy this expecting the same quality experience and I don't recommend anyone does that.) Also, I'm a bit disappointed they took out the collectables. I thought they gave the game a bit more replayability. This one feels about as straightforward as it gets. If you think you'll like it still, give it shot.

game_name: Cronos: The New Dawn - Deluxe Edition
review_text: Review from a Survival Horror Fanatic. Is it gonna scratch the Dead Space itch? A bit, it honestly makes me want to play DS again. Is it as good as Bloober's Silent Hill 2 Remake? No but that's okay! It's a great step in the right direction for Bloober Team and it could be an awesome series. The Horror aspect for me personally needs improvement and that's with my headset loud enough to cause hearing loss. The combat 8/10. Setting 9/10. Atmosphere 8.5/10. Horror 7.5/10. It really shines with keeping the situation tense but falls a little short on the scares. Resource management for survival horror experts will be easy but for casual players decently difficult. Overall I'm enjoying it and I can't wait to see where Bloober Team goes from here. 9/10 for me.

game_name: Cronos: The New Dawn - Deluxe Edition
review_text: Brutal? Absolutely. Visually and narratively interesting? 100%. Post-apocalyptic Poland, crawling with grotesque and horrifying abominations, low on resources, and full of intrigue and mystery. You'll probably die, a fair bit, but each time, pick up a bit of info about your foes and environment, and you'll see results when you use it to your advantage. Conserve ammo, but don't rely on melee, it's a last resort, unless you're skilled enough to make use of it. Don't panic, don't get cornered. Highly recommend for fans of Resident Evil, Dead Space, and Metro type games.

review_title: The "There's not enough resources" is a lie.
review_text: There's a TON of reviews claiming the game doesn't give enough resources, and it definitely does. They're more than likely not looking around enough or spamming/not charging shots, but there's 100% enough if you use your surroundings, properly manage resources, and don't spam every shot. - With that out the way, the game is fun and interesting. At first you'll be lost about the plot/story, but after reading the files you find and just by playing, it will unravel itself and you'll get the picture. - The gameplay is pretty similar to The Callisto Protocol (the enemies mutating, resource management, etc) just without a dodge mechanic (the movement helps save this). - The combat is fun and keeps you on your feet. The atmosphere keeps you on edge. The enemy designs are awesome. I've played alot of survival horror (every Resident Evil, Dead Space, etc) so maybe my review might count for something. If you love survival horror, this is worth grabbing. 100% recommend.

review_text: I played the first on the switch, kind of an arcade Armored Core. It had it's own personality and had tight level design and controls and a consistent art style that worked for it. This game feels like they had the ground work for a generic live service game and decided to slap on this name and make it mech centered because a CEO saw memes of AC6 all over the internet a few years ago and thought, "Nows the time! Mechs! Make it quick and get it out!" It's a 360 game that also crashes, has bugs and is priced like a modern game. It plays like Temu AC6: bad lock-on, AI, weapons, sound design, movement and took 'insperation' from the grindy monster hunter mechanics. They threw a little bit of everything in and watched it run down the wall and decided it stuck: mining, vehicles, card games, racing, fetch quests, escort, defense, open world, coliseum, crafting, base upgrade, ability crafting, randomized loot. Think Xenoverse 1. A rushed prototype that has potentioal but was *** out too soon.

review_title: This is NOT an action game
review_text: Do not go into this game thinking it's some kind of arcade off-road racer. SnowRunner is a slow-paced offroad SIMULATOR. You are tasked with completing deliveries or recovering lost supplies and vehicles. The challenge and fun comes from besting your adversary - the ground. You WILL get stuck in the mud and snow, and you WILL spend 10 minutes kicking yourself while you struggle to winch yourself out. Once you reach your destination, you're given some money as a reward - money that can be used to buy and upgrade your trucks. Rinse & Repeat. Is SnowRunner slow? - Yes Is SnowRunner boring? - A little bit Is SnowRunner fun, rewarding, and addictive? - ABSOLUTELY Final Note: I really hate most of the menus and the Garage/vehicle storage system is just awful, but those are really my only complaints.

Some areas are larger than others, and combat is fun, granted I'm not really struggling. You can kill enemies fairly quickly. You don't level up, or allocate skill points. There is also a lot of backtracking to open new areas later on with newly acquired keys or codes, just about EVERY door or chest needs a key or code to open. There are no "free" chests in this game. There is also NO MAP or guide holding your hand either. You must think, remember, and observe everything. It is a bit annoying, but overall I'm enjoying the game.

You're equiped with a sidekick as well that provides up to four different supports. There are a few consumables that will help you. review_title: Excellent game, beautiful, with its share of flaws.
review_text: This is the truest example of an action adventure game, honestly close to a gold standard. Game is highly polished, with few bugs to speak of, some areas have geometry issues where the lack of jumping can force you back to the main menu. Speaking of which, this is not a souls like or roguelite, death doesn't halt progression, and enemies dont respawn unless you leave the location. This game's main plot is nothing to write home about and the combat can grow stale by the late game, but there is something so compelling about everyone you meet, help, and talk to, that makes this game feel human. The world building is astounding, how they were able to fit millennia of background and story into each location seems highly difficult, even if the game isn't super ambitious. Graphics wise, just gorgeous, from dark hazy forests to wide open vistas, ancient castles and even a war torn city, each location is hand crafted and unique. Im out of words, buy this game. The VA for Adam Jensen is Remi.

review_text: This game is good, but short of great. All classes and abilities are quite enjoyable, and the levels are varied in look, as well as feel. Aside from that, many achievements are incredibly boring grinds: the one that made me quit was heal 1,000 times with food. I got literally every other achievement, and was under halfway for that. review_title: Overall pretty good but there are some big issues
review_text: The game itself is very fun to play, with or without friends. The only problems I have with the game are, the performance issues, the aim assist, and the lack of the customization the pc version has. During certain points in the game, the game's frame rate will all of a sudden tank even with the graphics setting turned to "performance favorable." Most notably on Tabletop, Museum, and Reality. The most common spots where the frame rate drops seem to be the middle of the map. The issue with the aim assist is that it will lock on to random enemies if they're close together, and when I say lock on I mean it. Multiple times I have aimmed at someone with their teammate nearby, the aim assist will lock onto the other enemy even if I was already shooting the other enemy. Now the lack of setting customization, more graphic, video, audio, and just basic setting options are very much needed. The game is still very fun but I recommend either not buying this until it is fixed or getting it on pc.

review_text: A sudden curfew has been issued in the small town of Little Creek. It's not normal, nor will the night be as Sloane and her friends sneak out to find out why. It's not long before you'll be exploring the town, solving puzzles and dealing with monsters. The town itself is set up well with many paths blocked off until you acquire keys or tools to get past a specific type of obstacle for example. While playing through it, it felt like a Goosebumps version of Resident Evil. Puzzles aren't overly complicated and some will have you sneaking, running away and hiding from monsters as you explore interior locations, gathering pieces for their solutions. You're also not totally helpless as you'll get a sling shot with different types of ammo to fight back or distract with. This was surprisingly longer than I expected and all characters are fully voiced. Achievements are very easy but there are two endings so two playthroughs for them all. The $40 is a bit high so grab on sale and have fun.

review_text: Feels like a classic from the PS2 days, for better and for worse. Traversal is a blast, between surfing on your shield and gliding through the air, mastering movement is very rewarding. You have a reasonably robust set of tools, but most of them either aren't rewarding enough when you compare it to just blocking to build super bar and nuking everything, or just aren't functional enough to bother with. Music is overall very pleasant and fitting. Lots of jank. Shield throw feels awful which is a huge shame since the animation in general is so fun and expressive, but the lock-on barely works and the frustration is compounded with it being the only way to incapacitate what is already the most annoying enemy in the game, who also happens to be unkillable for seemingly no reason. The story isn't anything too deep but the writing and scenarios were usually pretty funny and always charming. Definite mixed bag but overall positive experience. review_text: ALARM! Saw the PC version on YouTube and so glad it's here. You can feel the love put into this game if you're a Das Boot fan... review_title: Boring IF you have to play twice - 10/10 45min review:
review_text: CStP is basically missile defense with a splash of space invaders. There are rogue elements here like 3 skill choices after every wave (60 waves in total) and a skill tree you can buy buffs in, via coins you pick up in the run. There are 4 levels to choose from each with their own biome/environment . The way the HP works is 2-fold. The truck has hp and the conductor does as well (less than the truck) and you'll get HP pickups as you kill enemies. I did not die nor need to buy buffs, and got all 10 achievements by finishing ghe first level, having had bought each band member through the run. While CStP isn't bad at all and frankly I like the art style, it's just a bit easy, and given its manual shooting due to the Left-to-Right formula it get tedious holding left stick up constantly for such little impact. It's a slightly above average achievement game with custom art. At ToR I got it on sale for 1.74 USD and I'd say that to upwards of 3 USD is a fair price range for AH'ers.

review_title: A Contra Clone with a Health-bar!
review_text: I may be in the minority when it comes to this, but something that's always bugged me about Contra and Contra-clones alike is the fact your dude can only take one hit. Crushborgs however gives you health-bar right off the bat and vertical-platforming stages don't kill you when you drop down a platform; you just land! I realize this game is just a quick little BGM experiment for Darkman007 and Xitilon and an Achievement Hunter cashgrab, but just playing a Contra clone with a health-bar is a wish I've always wanted since I played the first Contra. Maybe this isn't the only Contra clone to do that and maybe this review will get 'actual-ied' and down-voted into oblivion, but I don't care: this game proves to me there is some hope left in this nostalgia-blinded corner of the industry. Damn good soundtrack, too; it all just makes ME happy.

review_title: A nostalgic blast from the past!
review_text: This gem of a game needs more love as it truly pays homage to the late Buichi Terasawa (RIP). A majority of the story is based on the 1982 anime. Even the cutscenes from in-game are taken from the anime as well. Space Adventure Cobra's story is very rich sci-fi fantasy during its time period. Anyway, this game really focuses on run & gun gameplay. A good tip would be to continuously shoot your psycho-gun ahead of you off screen. The music also sounds awesome and reminiscent to the anime. Though my only complaint would be trying to manually direct Cobra's psycho beam. Even with aim assist turned on/off it can sometimes veer into a nearyby enemy/switch when you're trying hit another enemy/switch. Which can be a little annoying. Though I wish the end boss in mission 13-1 got a cooler death animation (or anime cutscene) by getting blasted into space just like in the anime, as the in-game one felt anti-climatic. Now I feel like re-reading the mangas and rewatching the movie, anime & OVA's!

review_text: This game has immediately become a fixation of mine. As other reviews have mentioned there's a bit of a difficulty spike at chapter three, but after a few swings at it I finally broke through. I followed this up immediately with an unstoppable run in chapter 4. I felt powerful, like God must feel when he's holding a gun. Unfortunately when I set the game down at level 9 to grab dinner and watch Hulu, I came back to find the game completely unresponsive at the shop screen I left off on. I tried all the button mashing my caveman brain could muster to try and get it going again, with no luck. I had no choice but to quit and relaunch the game and lose all my progress. My RNG on subsequent attempts has paled in comparison to that god run. It's unfortunate because I'm otherwise really enjoying the gameplay loop, but a game like this should feel like you can safely put it down and pick it back up on a whim for long sessions or just a level or two. Hopefully this is fixed.

review_title: A Must Play For Souls Combat Enthusiasts
review_text: This is one of the better souls-like games if you're a fan of Bloodborne's combat mixed with Sekiro. There are 3 types of Blocking, one is your normal hold LB to negate all damage at the cost of stamina. Second is tapping LB the moment an attack lands to deplete the enemy's posture slowly, whereas the third block is a RIPOSTE which happens if you hold LB and attack at the same time an enemy hit lands, causing you to straight up rip their guts out. That visceral feeling of combat, combined with the fact that you have a Pistol that can also parry enemies is straight up from Bloodborne which I love so much. The level design and enemy variety isn't anything extraordinary, but for a $30 title it is pretty solid. The bosses are not easy, however they do not have any crazy AOE spam attacks so if you're any good at souls-games then you won't have much trouble with them. All in all, a great game to play if you love Fromsoft Titles. ðŸ‘Œ

review_text: Who would have thought the Prince of Persia series would make for a great metrovania style game. Well, that's exactly what happend. The combat is pure joy, the traversing is fun, although some may struggle later on because it gets pretty tricky and tough juggling all your time powers while avoiding the pits and traps. The bosses are great, enemy variety was knocked out of the park. You can make pretty interesting builds with the amulet system as well. My favorite is one where i equip 3 amulets to turn my bow into a deadly flaming shotgun bow, shooting 5 flaming arrows for the cost of only 1 in a broad sweep. This game is also longer than your typical indie metrovania. I'm clocked in at 36 hours and still haven't beat it. I would highly recommend this game to metrovania fans. review_text: This game caught my eye and as i love roguelikes, i had to try. It is very ambitous but misses the mark in some key areas. The main 4 power alternatives are interesting. The best is angelic and feels like a no brainer. The worst is the oil. Its the only one that actively hurts you and the enemies. They MIGHT fall but you slow down and lose friction on it. And if it catches fire (and it will) good luck. I really enjoy tweaking my exact combo but some options feel sluggish and weak. The flourish might work on paper but in reality costs you precious time. Time you don't have as there is sometimes HORDES of enemies on your screen. There in fact is so many with individual attack animations that trying to combo without a stagger or knockback is futile. And your dodge feels measly. It can be 5 stars with tweaks and i hope so

game_name: Daemon X Machina: Titanic Scion Demo
review_text: The control scheme is unusual, but makes sense after some time with it. Movement speed is crazy fast in boost (LS), and is even faster with light-weight mech suit parts... and it gets even faster than that with better gear. The game doesn't tell you this, but you can break red crystals or "femto containers" for your boost and flight fuel. The character customization options are robust, if weird. Mech appearance customization was excellent. Clever use of decals can make for cool patterns. Mech part customization is also extensive, and itemization seems good overall, but this is a demo. Who knows? Accidentally waking a colossus was both fun and briefly terrifying. I didn't try multiplayer. The writing is not it's strongest point, but the gameplay was fun enough to keep me for 4.5 hrs without noticing.

review_title: Good but not like the first
review_text: This game doesn't really have the same feel as DL1, less of a horror game and more of a standard RPG feel, that is somewhat dissapointing. Overall though not terrible, there are some bugs with the audio and visual but a lot of that's being fixed. Story isn't quite like the first but the voice acting is a bit better and the amount of actions you can take that change the course of the story makes for better replayability than DL1. The vs zombie combat feels worse than DL1 but, their recently updated weapons system is slighty better than DL1. The vs human combat on the other hand is improved from DL1, guns also feel better. Their are some good and bad things they added to parkour and whether you like that or not is largely personal preference. Overall, I think the biggest con in this game is it doesn't have that DL1 horror feel we all know and love. All in all, I would wait for a sale but still worth a playthrough or two, just don't expect the DL1 feel.

review_title: Should've been called Gates, Bridges, and Platforms
review_text: I don't mind puzzles, but these are not puzzles - they're simply exercises. The same mundane 'raise platform' 'unlock door' routine again and again and again. And the game tells you exactly what to do, so you're not even solving problems. It's dull, plain and simple. I thought these 'flip the door switch' games went out of style in 2005. As far as the narrative, kudos to the voice acting. It's all very well-done. Unfortunately, there isn't much of a 'story' being told, because you spend your time walking a straight path a raising platforms. Combat. While not dreadful, this isn't a game that has great collision physics, making combat (as well as other basic movement in the game) feel janky and not precise. The game looks pretty, although it's often hard to tell where you can and cannot go. The boundaries look the same as the environment - just gotta stumble around and get lucky. Echoes isn't the worst game you could play, but not all that good.

So I advanced past him and got to the second boss area. This boss proved to be incredibly challenging and I about threw my controller away, then I remembered what type of game I was playing.
