review_text: Heretic and Hexen are very important games that paved the way for in depth story telling in FPS games. Until these games, the plots to FPS were very limited in both in game and supplimental material. There was a lot of back story to them compared to even DOOM. Also the games gave proper names to the playable characters. Sure there was BJ from Wolfenstein, but the Heretic/Hexen games had a full named playable cast. The Heretic isn't just Heretic, he is Corvus. The playable classes in Hexen also have names and fleshed out back stories in ways that DOOM and Wolfenstein didn't have until more recent games. So instead of complaing just enjoy the games and the ability to play these important parts of gaming history. . .also if the devs try to remaster Heretic 2. . .please don't. . .instead remake the game from the ground because I for remember what a nightmare and slog that was to play 'cause the control layout for keyboard was that horrible no matter what.

review_text: Return to Moria has the great lore of LOTR, fun gameplay, cratfting, and restoration building, combat, co-op or single player. For 20 dollars it is great value these days with good graphics, and huge underground world to explore and restore, and endless gameplay. The mining is fun, crafting great, you can build anywhere you place a hearth, the character creation is good with many options, to make your Dwarf unique. As you restore Dwarven statues you unlock crafting recipes, and as you collect other items you unlock treasures. Digging through dirt walls opens new areas to find rare minerals, and gems. Between this game and the new Shire game coming this Fall we have new ways to experience the The Lord of The Rings world. Return to Moria is a rare gem with addictting gameplay that will keep you playing late night, and for months.

The best thing about this game is the presentation. There are some memorable music tracks and the graphics are created very competently, even if I found most of the character and enemy designs to be uninteresting. The gameplay leaves much to be desired, with boring combat that does not evolve at all throughout the game and movement abilities that are restrictive and limit player expression. Bosses feel unpolished and rarely have more than 2-3 attacks. For example there is an early boss that has a total of 2 attacks both of which it takes long enough to recover from that you can heal fully every time, making the boss almost impossible to die to. The level designs are usually a straight path to the boss with a few dead end paths with items and optional encounters which would be fine in a level based game but feels counter-intuitive in a Metroidvania. The game also is buggy, for example pop in and unwanted text being added to descriptions. Play The Last Faith or Blasphemous first.

review_title: Indie Devs dispelling the Gaming Dark Ages...
review_text: ...one bouncy bodacious beatdown at a time. Maiden Cops draws its inspiration from legendary titles like Streets of Rage and Final Fight. The gameplay really feels like SOR3 with the dodge roll and the rechargeable special meter amongst other things. Visually the game is excellent, with modern tech giving polish to retro inspired pixel art. Combat is fun and rewarding with each character having their own unique stats and play style. Meiga Holstaur is slow, yet strong, Priscilla Salamander is the balanced option of the three, and Nina Usagi is quick and agile. Each of them has three special moves which you'll want to mix in with basic attacks and wall bounces to get those gold tier combo scores. The writing was also very enjoyable with dialogue full of humor and charm. I did not encounter any glitches through my playthroughs, and with unlockables and gold scores to aim for, there's still much to do. Thank you devsðŸ‘

review_title: Strong underlying game with room to grow
review_text: More 4.5 stars than 5 as of right now. Pros: Nails the blend between a pick-from-3 roguelike and a simplified X-Com/Tactics experience. Good straightforward gameplay and a tough but manageable difficulty curve. Cons: Not quite optimized for console, shows in a handful of UI quirks. You can't easily reference what powerups you currently have. Also a little light on content in terms of build options and metaprogression. Overall, if the idea of the game sounds fun to you, it's worth it for $15 and if they continue to push updates then the foundation is strong enough to see this maybe becoming a standout title in the genre.

review_text: I had this cozy game on my wish list for months.So, it's safe to assume I was excited for this release. The game has a lot of potential to be great, but there needs to be some improvements. The camera zoom in and out as you move around in your house is nauseating for anyone who is sensitive to that. Moving around the village by guide of birds that seemingly blend in with the world will have you running in circles and constantly checking your map, breaking game immersion. Cooking feels unpolished with getting a mish-mash of goo in a bowl that somehow turns into a meal. There's straight confusion on the cooking goal, because it lacks explaining how you need to manipulate the preparation process to achieve a perfect meal via a gold icon inside of a taste chart. Feeding Hobbits a favorite meal is 100% guess work, and will have you frustrated. Decorating is nice and fleshed out, but seems it was more setup for PC play than console. review_title: I hated it at first. Now I love it.
review_text: Ive played all Dark Souls, Elden Ring, Nioh 1 and 2, Lies of P, Wo Long, Lords of The Fallen, Another Crab, Ninja Gaiden, Khazan, etc. This game is actually really good. Admittedly, I think they do a very poor job of explaining the mechanics. They use so many words to explain very simple things, which makes it confusing. That being said, I think some of the bosses have design flaws. One of them is designed around parrying, which is only one of many many abilities in the game, and the parry animation is very slow. So, is this a bulked up Logic Paint S? No! Not at all. This is it's own thing, most things vary between the two. First up, the illustrations. After each puzzel in the original, you got an illustration with the thing you made in the image. Here, that's not the case. Instead, you get costumes to put on the vocaloids, along with room items. Illustrations are now completion rewards for special puzzels and completing a characters set of puzzels. Speaking of... No reused puzzels (besides the hairpin lol). Everything is new. You get 5 10x10's, 30 15x15's, and 25 20x20's for the 6 vocaloids. Each one has 5 special puzzles 75x75 in length. You get 3 "other" 100x 100's as well. Stars also work different... ...Kinda. Clear the puzzel, use no hints, and clear with less than 3 mistakes. Those are the goals to hit. Use em' to get songs. And those are all new too! No oldies! Oh, and theres a hard mode if you turn puzzle assist off. That's all. Glory to Miku. I will endure for her.
Did the math, roughly ~1225 INDIVIDUAL puzzles, and that's JUST the base game content. DLCs add more. If you want a pefect way to kill time, this is your game to do it on.

More of 3.5/5 than 4/5, at ToR I'm in the 1% that maxxed all 22 character trees so hear me out: Something you need to know about SS is it has an artificial soft-cap to progression, as well as a hard cap. Each char can be leveled infinitely but the skill trees (22) cap at 170 skill points each, with each 3-4 tiers offering a minor global char stat buff - that's not the issue though. REGARDLESS of you having 0% bonus XP, or + 400%, you will generally be between lvl 50-60 by end of area 1, and 200-230 at Overlord (the 2nd endless mode) zone 6 - this is because, frankly, the game is poorly optimized. The devs confirmed this soft progression cap on steam 1yr ago. This make each run of SS feel VERY monotonous and repetitive. It takes roughly 1hr30min to get each char to 170 with the 50% bonus rune - huge time sink. Follow these tips though: Disarray>Shattered>Brittle>Fragile Doom>Bleed>Poison>Fire Overall SS has amazing features, but poor execution. It's evoled Army of Ruin, NOT Vamp Surv.

review_text: With 50+ hours total spend on Thomas and Bob, I can positively say this game is a hidden gem for turn-base RPG gamers. The inmates and setting are filled with entertainment pop culture and classic prison movies references, which put a nostagic smile on my face. The minigames can be confusing at first, but you can surpass them with enough practice for extra money. The time-passing and deadline essence of the game haven't given me issues since I'm experienced in time management games from games like "Frostpunk" and the "Persona" series; this mechanic may frustrate to some, but it's not impossible if you plan ahead. There is also action-based dice rolling elements like in Disco Elysium, but sadly you can't save scum manual saves if you fail a check. The combat itself is challenging at the beginning and end segments of the game, so train, make inmate friends, and prep your gear. Lastly, the soundtrack is banger and I can't wait to come back to this game as the upcoming third protagonist!

My Friendly Neighbor is like if Sesame Street met Resident Evil. Sticking to the survival "horror" genre, this game heavily emphasizes resource management and puzzle solving. Most of the puzzles weren't too hard and often times gave an "Aha!" moment when solving ones that left you stumbling around. The environments were beautiful and dark as if truly feeling like an eerie abandoned lot. Contrary to the good, "bosses" each had a gimmick and some were less clear than others on how to "defeat" them. I keep this vague as to not spoil anything as it is truly an enjoyable experience but because of this design it caused the pacing to feel off. Outide of this one issue, the other problems aren't nearly as weighted and purely instance based. Overall, I score it as a 4.5/5 Stars and recommend buying it as $30 is a very fair price for what it offers.

review_text: I have really been enjoying the experience. So, what makes this game Unlike Anything Else is, First: You're village that you build from scratch is always moving, you have to work with your Onbu, which is awesome because its extra to manage! ...with some bizarre controller layout decisions and very limited options to change them. For example, a one button photo mode that stops the game to take pictures on the left stick, with no option to change, and run\dodge on one button on the shoulder. I went from being skeptical about the concept to 100%'ing it. Crossplay online co-op and great voice cast. Important tip: Don't mash the dash button, time it. During a dash you're invulnerable so rather than frantically trying to escape an enemy's attack zone, time your dash to precisely avoid the frames you would have taken damage. That efficient use of dashing keeps you on cooldown less often and will help with survival.

Let us dispense with the pleasantries. I, your humble yet discerning narrator, have subjected myself to the digital crucible of Volcano Princess. One might be tempted to dismiss it as mere child's play, but to do so would be a grave error, a testament to one's own intellectual improverishment. The graphics, initially charming in their simplistic way, soon become a source of creeping dread. The blank, soulless eyes of the digital princess stare into your soul, judging your every failure. The soundtrack, a cacophony of gurgles, whimpers, and high-pitched screams, burrows its way into your subconscious, never truely leaving you. The true horror lies not in the gameplay, but the atmosphere. The game creates a pervasive sense of dread, a feeling that you are being watched, judged, and slowly consumed by something melevolent. Volcano Princess is not for tHe faint of hEart. it's a game that wiLl test your limits. if you dare Play, do so at your own risk. you May never be the samE...

review_text: I'll admit up front that there are, of course, better examples of souls games on the market (Elden Ring, Dark Souls 3, Bloodbourne). There are also better non-fromsoft souls games (Wo Long, Lies of P, Khazan). Indeed, there are better sci-fi souls game too (The Surge 2, Hell is Us, Remnant 2). There are even better cutesouls, tho not very many (Kana, Little Witch Nobeta, Another Crab's Treasure). But there's something about this game. It feels...personal. Intimate. Non-derivative. Almost like it's someone's off-clock experiment. It's got charm, and even a little gravitas. And despite not being a huge game, the level design feels intentional in a way that makes it feel far bigger than it. And like the games listed above, and all good souls games, it does an excellent job of rewarding exploration in such a way that you want to look under every rock and behind every tree. It feels like the people who made enjoyed making it; as though they made the game because they enjoyed it.

review_text: The game starts reasonably well, and the setting is interesting, but it leaves you wanting more. PROS: Art style, level design, boss fights, difficulty options. CONS: Repetitive combat, lacking enemy variety, half-baked story. OKAY: Crafting/upgrading, the MITT gameplay mechanic, lore. Worth mentioning that this game has a Hero mode (easy) and a Master mode (hard); one feels like a cakewalk, while the other feels like a souls game. The difference is based on how much damage enemies deal to you and how fast they attack, with parries being required on Master difficulty. When you learn why it's called "Robots at Midnight", don't think too highly of it; I initially got a Dying Light vibe only for it to leave me incredibly underwhelmed by it being scripted. This game took me about 8 hours to beat, which isn't great for $20. Definitely wait for a sale. Overall, it's fine. Just remember that this is an indie game though.

Nice player base. Questing is good solo or with a group. Stay away from this game before you dump to much hard earned money to be able to walk away. The development team only cares about seperating you from your paycheck & some even openly mock you on social media for having any kind of feedback that doesn't agree with them.

review_text: 1975. Isolated in an ocean of cutting grey water is a Scottish owned oil rig, Beira D. Cameron McCleary, a newbie electrician is called to his bosses office in regards to a mishap back home that took place shortly before his arrival. After an exchange of words, Caz is told to leave. Right before he's able to, a catastrophic malfunction rocks the rig and it's workers. As a result, a mysterious eldritch force is awoken, threatening the sanity and very lives of the personnel aboard the Beira D oil rig. Cut off from the outside world and armed with nothing more than his wits and companions, Caz must find a way off of this doomed rig in order to make it back safely to his dear family. How far is a man willing to go in order to preserve his life? What is he willing to do for the people he cares about? What is he willing to sacrifice?

review_title: It Is What It Is, And It Ain't No More
review_text: I mean it's not a remaster, so don't go into it expecting modern graphics. It's pretty much exactly the same as it was back in the day, and that's not at all a bad thing. There are a few neat things like special features, a CRT filter and cool screen borders to switch through. By and large though it's 30 bucks to conveniently play the old trilogy through your Xbox, it's up to you if you're down for that or not. As someone whose Gex 3 disc was badly scratched, lost and has no working N64 or original PlayStation to play this on, I am DEFINITELY not regretting this purchase. And I can't even rate it lower than a 5/5, because even if a newer, younger player doesn't dig the outdated graphics or sometimes wonky 90's gameplay then that doesn't mean there's actually anything wrong with this game. For what it is (a port) it checks every box. If you had complaints about Gex back then, then you'll still have those complaints now. If you loved Gex back then, then you'll love it now. I dig it. ðŸa°

This is a pure stealth, modern thief simulator. You must avoid detection, and cannot harm or kill your way in or out. You must drive janky cars, weave your way between people and cameras on foot, sometimes even run like hell and hide, and use that brain of yours to work out a viable sequence of actions to solve each puzzle. I had no problem beating this game, there were no bugs big enough to break it for me, and the only reason I stopped playing is because of the pure stealth aspect. 35 hours, compared to the hundreds I have logged on Payday 2 while completing similar enough activities. If you can meet it where it's at and accept it for what it is though, you just might be able to enjoy your time with this game, every bit as well as I have. Seriously, I still want to play it again some time. But I like stealth, janky driving, and reverse Santa Clausing everything that isn't nailed down. I'd suggest ignoring all the bad reviews, if this game has what you're looking for. Enjoy!

A monster shows up some, benign and not scary. There's kind of a story? It's very bad. The prison is not a convincing prison (maybe if you're a teenager that just watched 'The Rock' or some prison reality TV shows). There's details that make no sense (BTC transactions but the tech involved in the prison is 90"s at best?) The "story" there is goes in too many directions with no personal involvement. Each letter interacted with only lends to further convolte other details. There is no challenge, either. Given a door that needs a 4 digit code, you find the code in a note. Instead of challenging the gamer to remember the code, it is then prominently displayed on the screen.

review_title: Massive Potential, Huge Playerbase to tap into.
review_text: You guys have phenomenal bones here, and the gameplay appeals to trucking sim AND space sim playerbases. If I were in the position to suggest something, it would be interior space stations first and foremost. Let us go inside to buy supplies and secure contracts. It's ALL about immersion with a game like this. Make us get out and pump our gas. Give us showrooms to walk through and buy trucks from. Overall you guys are absolutely on the right track, just keep fleshing it out and most importantly adding depth.
If you're playing the 'Recommended' difficulty you're doing it wrong. Custom is where its at. Turn down air filter and battery drain and hit the space road. You're welcome. ðŸ ̃Ž
Been wanting a space sim like this for years. I'm always a hauler in any space game I play, from Elite to Starpoint to Rebel Galaxy to Starfield. I'm finally legit space truckin'...

This is way more fun than it has any right to be. Playing it with the custom settings. (Low maintenance, high payouts)... Very satisfying and a great chill and vegetate game. 1000 cool points awarded to the cool cats who made this.

Bit of a learning curve, but I see the potential. Game's designed for you to chill and drive in outer space. Just be patient and take it slow. Remember, the docking camera is your best friend when attempting to load a trailer or dock somewhere.

Okay, so when i downloaded this on gamepass, it was mainly just out of curiosity. The concept seemed cool and unique so i booted it up thinking id play for like 5 mins then uninstall it. But HOLY MOLY i was instantly hooked. I loved Hardspace: Ship Breaker which feels like where the inspiration for this game came from so it felt very familiar right off the bat. Which is great! i havent found any other space game that gave me that Ship Breaker feeling so strongly. BUT.. Holy Dingdangdaroo. Ive died so many times to the air filters that im starting to get frustrated with them. The rate they drain your cabin's oxygen if you only have 1 left is INSANE. You basically have to spend huge chunks of your payouts on stocking filters since they can cost up to $3000 EACH. To fill 4 SLOTS? FREAKING WUT? Oh and BTW, not every store has them so have fun remembering which ones and choking on the way there. Lol Jeez man, i get im not the best at planning ahead, but the filters are way 2DEADLY.

If you seen that movie then you will nerd out as hard as I when I first saw this, controls take time to get used to and the inverted control seems so natural compared to most flight controls now and days. All in all great and fun game so far.
If you get this you're a god d*mn legend. "See ya, space cowboy".

Real-life OTR truck driver here, this game is addicting and unironically realistic. Thanks to the devs for making the bed functional for well deserved naps, now we just need a way to get coffee and/or energy drinks. Also, can you add new/more trucks and maybe add some form of interior customization? We have that massive dash but no bobbleheads nor Cowboy Hats to put on it. Keep up the good work Devs, thank you for this awesome product!!!

Idk, I was really excited for this game. Loved the demo and was hoping it would be expanded on a lot up to release. The visuals are nice and I really like the tactile sense of having a lot of switches and buttons to press in your cab. Unfortunately, the novelty wears thin pretty quickly. There isn't much Trucking. You get a job, pick up trailer, drive to warp gate, go to next hub. There isn't a lot in the sense of "Hauling". No 6DoF. This was genuinely baffling. The true game is managing your truck. Power cells. They run all your trucks systems, drain relatively fast, are expensive, and are just a pain to deal with. It really takes away from the open road, trucking experience when you're near constantly worrying about managing power in your truck. The truck itself is also made of Aluminum foil. One hit will turn your rig into Swiss cheese. And honestly not a big deal, but irked me, is there is only one radio station that cycles the same 5 or 6 songs. The game just isn't there yet.
If you are not blasting Deep Purple's "Space Truckin" from the live Made in Japan album or The Grateful Dead's " Truckin' ", you're doing it wrong.

You can tell this was made by a passionate team with all the small details and care in the design of the world and interactions. Pretty sure this was made for me. It's a trucking game so know what you're getting into. Great job devs!

No, everyone leaving less than a 5 star review isn't just scared of a challenge... The game has a great foundation but some things are pointless annoyances. For one, the damn hood of the truck takes up half the screen! Any time you need to gain elevation you're completely blind to anything infront of you, wouldn't flat nose models make more sense? Debris spawns in thin air directly infront of me yet all I can see is black space. Not asking for full visibility, just more than 40%...like tf? The oxygen glitches CONSTANTLY, as if constant repairs wasnt already enough, you will pass out when there's literally nothing wrong with any system. Annoying af and it forfeits your current job. I literally passed out in the tutorial on my second restart, full oxygen and filters...literally 3 minutes into my playthrough. Seems more like a ''tedious = difficult'' type game than I imagined. People need to understand that you're not cool for acting like every problem is just a skill issue.

Finally learn the enemies combos, deflecting is good and everything, but you have legs, and can outrun most of the enemies without worry, so take your time. The game maybe hard, but loot really comes in handy, use it to your advantage. And enjoy the game even when you die, because you will die, a lot. review_title: Relaxing. More Theme Park than PGA2K
review_text: This is a classic Kairsoft game. There is a low-skill threshold, you do not play golf, you just design and grow the course with simple drag and drop controls. It is a macro not micro-management game, you donâ€TMt have to hire staff, set prices or sculpt topography. The gameplay loops overlap beautifully, new holes need to balance difficulty with scenery to attract new members, advertising campaigns & tournaments boost players and, in a timing mini game you coach your players so they can win tournaments. All contributing to the requirements to rank up your club to the next star to unlock more course and clubhouse design options. It is a slow and somewhat therapeutic gameplay experience that will have you looking at your watch wondering how did this much time pass. It does not revolutionize the genre, but it does distill the expertise of developer who has done this many times and it makes for a great gaming sorbet between M Rated FPS and 100 hr RPG

review_title: One of my favorite puzzle games!!!
review_text: Previously played this game on PC and was blown away. Best described as a semi open world Portal game that has a deep philosophical story. Definitely recommended!!

Gameplay is in the style of Portal 2, The Turing Test and older Sherlock Holmes games by Frogwares. Also a bit like The Witness, but with abilities and more varied puzzles. Story is deeply philosophical. Existentialism, rationalism, empiricism and transhumanism. Also theology, mythology and artificial intelligence. Do you do what you are told? Or blindly follow those before you? Or rather do whatever you want instead? Graphics are decent and has quality or performance option. There are some frame drops when inside the elevators, but I assume this is due to loading/buffering. Music is very fitting for the atmosphere and changes with each hub/nexus. There are quite a few mutually exclusive achievements which will require multiple playthroughs or reloading. I completed the story and collected all sigils (not including stars) without any in-game hints or outside guide in 17 hours (in-game save, not Xbox time). YMMV depending on your outside the box thinking. I used a guide for stars.

If you love first person puzzle games, this is for you. It also looks gorgeous and has a greatly customizable photo mode. I see another review complaining about frame rate, and while I suppose that's fair, I ask myself how much I care about good frame rates in a non physics based puzzle game. The answer is not much. Especially not enough to drop a 1-star bomb like they did. If you enjoy puzzle games, I recommend trying this game for yourself. This version also comes with the DLC and a brand new chapter so there's plenty of value. If you really enjoy this there's also a sequel and a free prequel (only on PC) named Sigils of Elohim.

Closest game to Portal in the store. This title focuses on puzzle solving while driving a philosophical stoy line. There is no humor as was in the Portal franchise but it is deeply engaging. The puzzles arc in complexity nicely but never feel out of reach. I waffled on purchasing this one for awhile do to the price but this game is flat out awesome! Worth every penny.

The weapons are meh, mostly because the smg/ar are leaps above the rest since you get swarmed and their fire rate & reload times are more ideal for those situations. The sniper is nice, until the game locks you in a small space to fight. I had some bad fps drops in the later maps, nearly killing me since the game was not reacting in sync. I also got locked in an infinite loop of spawning enemies in a locked corridor and had to quit after 15 minutes of hoping the same 7 basic enemies would stop spawning and the red barriers would let me go. Overall, its fun and I only played solo, but it does need more weapons that are viable, espeically as the higher difficulties. Solo is quite hard with the locked in the small space wave attacks, but winning there feels great. Id say grab it on a sale, or wait for more content bit short

review_title: Intriging. Scary. But has its flaws.
review_text: It is rare that a game can grab my attention the way this one has. It usually takes a deep story, strong voice acting and solid gameplay. Emily Wants to Play is missing the first two and it does not matter. The game is all about survival. I did jump quite a bit. The scares were successful. Sometimes the anticipation of something happening was enough to keep me from even blinking. Of course in fear of being greeted by one of the house's inhabitants. My favorite aspect was figuring out what I had to do to survive until the next hour. This element was appreciated. Where the game fell a bit short was AI difficulty and load times. The game can be unforgiving at times when it starts to stack different rules. This is where load times come in. You can fail in seconds and have to wait close to 1 min for it to load. Rinse and repeat. It in no way hurt the experience too bad. But it can feel like a lot of waiting. For $5 this game is a steal. I recommend this game to anyone.

A major glitch that frequently cropped up was climbable ledges simply not registering, which for a platforming game is rough, forcing the player to reload a save only to have another ledge rendered unfunctional (Beyond Good and Evil from 20 years ago plays better). Combat and movement never mesh well and are incredibly clunky, seeming slow and disjointed. Most of the game is in love with its ideas, doting on specifics like the drone companion, but it really struggles with their implementation, level situations that should be challenging are lessons in unnecessary frustration (some of the forced combat sections are just tripe even knowing the mechanics). TLDR: It looks beautiful, feels like a classic title, but the techinical aspects of the game leave something to be desired; not really fun.

review_title: MercurySteam Struck While The Iron Was Hot!
review_text: Before anything else, the most important thing I can say is THANK YOU MERCURYSTEAM for making something new, and thank you to 505 for publishing it. The game itself revolves around attacking using all four face buttons for different directions in both light and heavy attacks. There's a heavy emphasis on making every weapon yourself (barring your first sword of course) and really tailoring your gameplay to your play style as you earn better metals and woods to work with and gather materials to fit those moulds. I really like the whole "kill each enemy type enough to earn their weapon blueprint" bit. I've just reached the Doyen Graves after a few hours of play and one particularly fun boss fight in a fortress, and while I wouldn't say the story is communicated in the clearest way from the start, I would say the characters are all interesting and funny in different ways! Don't sleep on this, it's worth the price of admission.

I've tried combinations of each faction and attempting unconventional strategies, but to get walled at the end after steamrolling through every previous fight, how does corruption feel anything but unfair? 20 strike damage, plus two corruption, plus doubling that corruption every turn is just too much. Everything before the final boss feels euphoric. There are challenge runs to try (separate from community runs), there's more story, twice as many factions, and mutators are back for you to create the ideal challenge run. Other may feel conflicted on the art, but the developers give each artist credit when you zoom in on a card, which I applaud.

review_title: Addicting deck builder / tower defense type of game
review_text: I got addicted to the game real fast and I loved the progression system. there's a few different decks with unique cards they all seem to be varied and I love how you unlock each hero.

On the artifact/card/resource/roguelike stuff it's basically a copy-paste of Slay the Spire, but that's fine because Slay the Spire is polished. The only difference is it changed Slay the Spire into a tower defense game (enemies advance several stages, only your towers (cards) at each stage can attack those enemies, enemies that make it to the end remove HP from your base which has to be kept alive. Main downside is it feels very short. A run might be 8-9 fights, but the first 2-3 fights are basically so simplified/basic that they don't really count. A run feels like maybe 3 actual fights that are a little significant. A Slay the Spire run feels 2-4x longer to me. Basically, by the time I've actually upgraded one or two units, gotten one or two sweet artifacts that are worth building a deck around and maxed one or two spells, the campaign is over before it feels like I really use them.

review_text: While the visual appeal is obvious, this game lacks the basics in other game designs that make a game fun and entertaining. Instead full of frustration and tedium. Gameplay is mobile game level at best. Simply put, the golfing in this golf game is basic with the absence of ball physics relative to swing power and the surface the ball is on. Finding the perfect swing angle and power level seems like a *** shoot. The game has no consistency with ball movement and momentum. While im sure some will find the radio station aesthetic interesting (the story), it became annoying after about the 10th hole. This seems trivial but i found it quite annoying. Restarting a hole isn't done quickly due to having to pause the game to the menu which is done through a graphical transition rather than instant. Some may not be bothered by this but after restarting over and over in challenge mode it can eat up some time. You also don't move your character. He moves on his own to the next shot.

There are puzzles, most of which aren't too hard but the piano one will test patience. Now this is a very dark game and you can adjust the brightness, it just has to be done from settings after you start playing. Brightness isn't an option from the start menu. Aside from some jank from controller inputs, everything does work. Achievements are 100% obtainable and easy to get in one short playthrough. Depending on your speed, it can take a few hours. I would suggest to the devs not to reveal so much in the trailer next time. Some elements could have had a bigger impact if left out. I am interested in the growth of what this developer comes out with next.

review_title: Honest review for people wanting to know about gameplay
review_text: First off, it is NOT pay-to-win. All microtransactions are cosmetic except one that gives your pet the ability to ship items every 10 mins. Some are gotten via Twitch or seasonal events for free. Game plays like Animal Crossing but anime humanoids, focusing on building and designing your own fantasy home and furniture. You hunt, catch bugs, fish, mine, and cut trees for materials to use or sell, buy upgrades and recipes, and garden and cook food for an exp boost to your skills. Everything can be done in groups except story quests. You also can date the NPCs to get more stat boosts. I personally don't have issues with the community in game, but I also am not in the Discord chats. Played on Switch 2 years ago and was glad to see my entire account and home ported over. That said, climbing can still be a chore and has needed tweeking since day 1, the map opens the shop if you try to use the same button to close it, and the fact you can't help people do quests you completed does stink.

review_text: It's cool, but much harder than Hotline Miami. You also have way more enemies to kill before each checkpoint (even in the 3rd level there's like 15 to 20 guys to kill in one life), less useful cover and a hard time telling what is cover and what isn't, no way to scroll the screen a bit (there's just red arrows to indicate enemy presence, but if you can't see if they're behind cover you don't know how to enter the room). Enemies also instantly sense you once you have line of sight of them, even if they have their back turned and are in a different room. The only way to get a drop on enemies is the dodge and slow-mo. It's cool someone decided to make a prettier Hotline Miami, but why did they think it had to be much harder too? The cheap needless deaths get annoying.

review_title: It does exactly what it sets out to do
review_text: This is not a bad game by any means. For me, I found the humor a little...young, and the combat a bit imprecise, but it all works fine, and the devs clearly had a vision, and they achieved that vision. If you like goofy, punny humor, and don't care about razor's edge precision in your arpg combat, then pick it up. I think i was hoping for more of an insider's lampooning of souls games, but it really has nothing to do with that. It's more about euro-style arpg tropes turned up to 11. In fact, you'll prolly enjoy the game more if you're not familiar with souls games, cuz you won't be comparing it to the flawlessly accurate melee combat and deep, organic exploration that you get from fromsoft. Which, to be clear, is a really unfair comparison to make. This is not a bad game by any means, and it's not trying to live up to dark souls. I'll prolly play some more when i'm in a goofy, childlike mood. And if you like goofy, frivolous humor, you'll probably love this. Just be aware what it is.

review_text: Game pace is too slow: Everything including movement speed, weapons, weapon upgrades, roguelike improvements, as well as enemies. Next, most augments come with both penalties and upgrades--especially, slower movement, reduced collection radius, less health, etc. As if the game wasn't BORING enough, the devs further stipled your plans at fun. 100% of deaths come from stacking debuffs to do more damage (risk / reward), then getting 1-shot at full-health on normal difficulty. Ive had runs where i felt immortal, killing enemies at screen edge, then died full health, not knowing how i died, or even why. This happens EVERY death. Theres also zero explanations on what crit hits do. Do they hit for 1.5 damage? idk. There's also something called brutal hits , which proc off crit hits. Do they hit for x10 dmg? idk & neither do the devs--else they would have told you in the TIPs menu. All in all, the game is a chore which doesn't reward you for your time.

First off, it is a very basic survivors game. Complete 8 maps and you can opt to fight a boss (click the icon in top left) that is so easy to avoid taking damage but you chip at so slowly that it took me literally 23 minutes to kill. Graphics look like they were drawn on Windows 98's MS Paint, but still can drop the frame rate to 0 on my Series S like Vampire Survivors does, only when VS does it there are about 20x more enemies on screen, which makes sense. Yes, you can upgrade a lot, but the upgrades aren't anything special (basic speed, damage, and range upgrades) and cost way too much for such little improvement. Case and point, one skill goes up by 0.5% each upgrade and you max them @ 100. By rank 50 you'll be doing a full level to afford that one 0.5% increase, and at rank 100 the increase is barely any improvement still. There are also microchips that do similar increases and you can equip and then farm, very slowly, gems and minerals to refine in order to upgrade those as well.

I've mashed the breaks in mid turn completly overshooting the turn and not wipeout, very forgiving. Vets just play on pro and crank up the Ai. Supermoto, flat track are a nice add on and a whole new set of skills to learn. Flat and supermoto does feel a bit floaty but not awful. Mini bikes are hilarous fun. Downside is only 2 tracks for the 3 extra modes. Hopefully they add more tracks for these modes. Graphics are the best yet. Customization and animations outside of races mostly remain the same. Overall if you're looking to get back into MotoGP this is the game to do it. When I get off the game I find myself wanting to get back and I haven't felt that in a long time. Oh yeah, split screen racing. Buy it!!!

review_title: Reminded me of why I love video games
review_text: Clair Obscur reminded me that video games are at their best when they are treated as art pieces, not products, being passionately worked on by a group of creative people, and not a board room full of executives that will throttle all the true joy and life out of a game for the sake of reaching a wider audience. Its not afraid to have real heart and emotion, it assumes its players are adults with actual attention spans, and man, all the artists absolutely went off. From the world to the music, the cut scene direction, the sound design, all of it is the glorious end result of people bringing their passion and drive into something they truly wanted to do. To me, the unexpected popularity of this game also shows solidification of a trend in the gaming industry; that AA and indie can now not only compete directly with AAA games but also clearly surpass them with fewer resources, due to the passion and drive that propels these smaller studios like Sandfall Interactive.

review_text: Do you enjoy tactical RPGs? How about couch co-op games? If you do, and you have a couple of friends who feel the same, you might enjoy this game! Sunderfolk plays like a simplified TRPG, where each turn you play a card that lets you move and attack with your character (1 of 6, each one with different abilities). You control your character using a mobile device with the goal of your party completing the mission objectives (kill monsters, save victims, interact with objects, etc.) After each mission, your party returns to town to level up, improve your character, talk to townsfolk, and other typical actions in a TRPG. The mobile device controller allows you to scan a QR code in order to resume progress between play sessions, and to edit your Fate/Action decks as you get new cards to improve your character. So far, we have been enjoying the game, and are looking forward to finishing the story!

review_text: I remember playing the original game on the xbox 360. I didn't really play again after skyrim came out. The one thing keeping me from playing oblivion again was the horrible leveling system. The remaster has simplified the stat system and now you can just play casually without being forced to micromanage your skill leveling to get the correct stats when leveling up. In the original, you needed 10 levels in a strength related skill to get 5 points in the strength attribute when you sleep to level up. If you didn't maximize to get 4-5 points in strength and endurance as a melee build each level, then you wouldn't be able to keep up with the difficulty increases as you reached higher levels. That forced you either power game, or just stay low level forever to keep the game from getting too hard. The remaster has made this into a more simple and relaxed leveling experience.

review_title: Best Silent Hill tribute in a long time.
review_text: I have been an obsessive Silent Hill fan since I was a child with 1-4 on PSX/PS2. Those games defined my taste in horror and surreal cinematic atmosphere, so let me be clear: This game gets it so right. The subway/mannequins/hospital vibe will be immediately familiar to SH fans, and it looks so good in UE5. The stilted voice acting and weird posters perfectly captures the dreamlike atmosphere of the originals, and the creators really use the fixed camera angles for maximum cinematic effect. Even the soundtrack sounds like golden age Yamaoka. As others have stated, combat is sporadic and the biggest focus is on the environmental storytelling and the classic horror puzzles, so if you prefer more of a slow-burn atmospheric surreal horror to nonstop action, this is right up your alley. If this was released as an official Silent Hill game I wouldn't have ever suspected otherwise. If you're as much of a fan as I am, you've seen these tropes many times before, but this one does them justice.

review_text: The people complaining that the puzzles are too hard, that there is no map system, that the controls are too clunky and that there isnt enough combat probably play mostly modern games that hold your hand the entire time and are nothing more than one giant action setpiece after the next. This game is very much rooted in the oldschool survival horror tradition. The most obvious influence being the old PS1/PS2 Silent Hill games, but with UE5 graphics, which mainly look very good. The game was made by a very small indie team on a budget, so there are some shortcomings and jagged edges here and there, graphically, technically and design wise. Still, it's remarkable what they were able to accomplish with the limited means they had. I'd like to see what they could do with more resources, as this is a very good puzzle and exploration oriented, psychological survival horror game in the old tradition. If that sounds like your thing, give it a shot, but keep in mind this is from a small dev team.

review_text: Not everyone will "get" this game, but for those who do, it is pure bliss. The same studio that brought you Paradise Killer has now used their amazing worldbuilding skills to bring you a story where humans exist alongside cartoonish and bizarre mascots, basically their own species, and you play as a disgraced Yakuza ace voiced by the legendary actor behind Kazuma Kiryu himself. In the first ten minutes a guy gets shot, another cuts off his own pinky, and you meet an anthromorphic finger running a love hotel, and that is just the world this game exists in. So, you're getting an open-world Yakuza style management sim with the amazing creativity of Kaizen behind it, with a dash of Deadly Premonition and the original No More Heroes thrown in. If that's your taste in games like it is for me, don't hesitate. This is your game.

For myself I just give up, I'm looking up solution after solution and saying: "I would never figure that out ever", because I don't understand somthing from outside the game. I love puzzle games and never have played a game anywhere near as cryptic as this. It should be a fun ride for most but once you hit "room 46" best of luck because the game ceases to be accessable to 99.9% of the population after that.

review_text: This is a game with real heart and soul. Take Alice in Wonderland and add a bit of southern comfort and you've got South of Midnight. The environment is incredible, with each level featuring rich and vibrant designs. The story is heart-warming and endearing, showcasing the love and bond between mother and daughter. The game itself isn't too dense, featuring somewhat challenging combat and platforming without too much frustration. It's a game I would recommend for anyone wanting to engage more with the story. Definitely one you can throw on to sit back and relax with. The combat, however, gets repetitive over time and is isolated to mainly small arenas. There also isn't too much variety in enemy types. That being said the fights are fun and fast paced while still giving you and the character plenty of mobility. The ending felt a bit rushed but I will admit it's more about the journey than the destination. Still recommend as a simple and entertaining adventure game!

The sticker system is a nice refreshing idea. You don't lose moves, you peel them off your monsters and can stick them back on to another if they are compatible. For a game that's being light-hearted, focusing on fun and laughs, it has a few surprisingly darker areas. I won't give anything away, but I will say it'll keep you hooked to the end. review_title: Somber Story. Satisfying Gameplay. Great Game.
review_text: This roguelike has gameplay like Warm Snow, but mechanics like Hades. Despite having an art style like Ashen, the vibe is more in line with Life Is Strange. In the real world you build relationships with characters, giving them gifts and chatting with them to learn more about them, as so they can provide buffs in the dream world. The dream world is the rogue loop: several layers/bosses deep, and about an hour long run to the end. Tons of weapons and boons to unlock as you progress. There is an easier difficulty option in settings, but enemies are no pushover in later zones. My only real complaint is that, playing this on my series s, it was causing my console fan to run a bit hard (comparably to something like a massive AAA game, such as Witcher 3). To my achievement hunters, be warned... This game is serious grind to unlock and do everything. Not as easy as other roguelikes, but still worthwhile. Also, this game is on sale regularly, so picking it up for around $5 is well worth it imo

review_text: Dollhouse has surprisingly been an IP for years, the first title going through some sort of developmental hell ages ago. I remember waiting what felt like a decade for the original to drop, and being quite disappointed when it did. I honestly wasn't expecting a sequel to even happen. The first was pretty bad, likely due to multiple factors including the split focus between single and multiplayer, though it had some good ideas. This follow up is a strictly solo affair and does manage to exceed the original in many ways, though not enough to really stand out unfortunately. I would advise against a full price purchase. In a world with the likes of Madison, Tormented Souls and Still Wakes The Deep, this simply doesn't rise to a standard worthy of its asking price. The controls are stilted, combat equal parts boring and frustrating, graphics are fine, occasionally nice but mostly by-the-numbers 'indie-horror'. If you really are curious, wait for a sale.

review_title: A Wonderful Fusion of Familiar Mechanics
review_text: I'll preface with an opinion; I have not beaten The First Berserker: Khazan yet, but this will most likely be my personal GOTY. This game [so far] has been a tour de force of game development. At it's core, it is a satisfying blend of punchy, frenetic combat, looping linear exploration, an interesting world, and light rpg mechanics. Sound familiar? For fans of the genre, it will be, and yet it's not entirely derivative for a genre so full of hits. Gameplay is a mix of parries, dodges, stance breaking, and special skills. The skill tree features a path for each of the 3 weapon types, one for shared skills, and one more, but that's a spoiler. The setting is very much dark fantasy. high castles, jagged peaks, dank caves, bandits and deadly monsters. Think of Kentaro Miuras work. The visual design is unique and beautiful, the music is tense and somber, and the voice acting is fantastic, especially from our duo protagonists. If you like this genre, play the demo, see what I mean.

The builds while not SUPER varied they get the job done and combos are very satisfying to do. The artstyle is nice too, and the stories that are told throughout the game not only fit with the art but they're very emotional too. Many of the characters are likeable and very few that are disliked. My gripes with the game are somewhat small but can make the game a tad repetitive. Such as the progression and missions are pretty linear, you can't really deviate apart from what you're given. And another small gripe is cutscenes are completely gone if you swap khazans gender. But apart from those i can't think of anything at the moment. If you haven't played the game yet i HIGHLY recommend it, it's a hella great game!

review_text: Yes, best, I said BEST! The First Berzerker: Khazan, offers a both unique but also familiar experience. The art style is completely unique, but I guess the best way to explain it is BOTW meets Sekiro with a manga feel. The games combat is reminiscent of Sekiro, Lies of P, and Bloodborne. The games other features, mainly item progression, is similar to nioh, with lots of variations of the games same 3 weapon types. The games map, while not open world, is also not entirely linear, offering different locations to chose to explore. The games progression of attributes is similar to classic fromsoft souls games, just at a slower place. It also uses lacrima (souls) as both currency and a method of leveling up, which you drop and can retrieve upon death. It has a skill tree similar to recent Assasins creed games, with unique abilities for each weapon type. Khazan has issues, no hard difficulty, gang fights, to much loot, etc. But overall, it's nearly perfect. A true 10/10 experience.

The cutscenes show little to no animation, bad pacing and editing choices lead to a stale boring experince. Instead of a comprehensive cinematic experience that retells the best parts of Bleach, we're given characters standing around expositioning cliffnotes around action but show nothing with. This is not a game that'll make new Bleach fans or completely satisfy old ones. It is a good fighting game, but not worth its price. -No og Bleach music ops ends or osts from the anime. -You can NOT play Orihime Inoue or Vizords other than Shinji. :( +og voice actors make a return but not all. review_title: Fun game that could have been better.
review_text: It's a fun game, but the amount of gold you can have is terrible. If there was no coin purse limit would be alot better, also they should have placed hidden better gear that you could wear instead of just upgradeing gear. Love the old school look and playstyle. If they decide to make another they should make no coin limit, much bigger inventory, more and bigger dungeons, and hidden better equipment and weapons that are not required to beat game. Overall was worth $7.50 price i paid when on sale.

CONS: If grinding is your thing go right ahead. EVERYTHING costs either half or all of your gold if you're maxed out. The item upgrades don't feel significant. Some of the mobs (I'm talking to you giant eyeball ghosts) are weirdly hard compared to other environment mobs. It's very hard to take in your surroundings and try to find 30 some-odd caves with 5 of these shooting balls at your back and another one every two inches. The hit boxes can be off and the puzzles take way too precise of movement for controls that feel cumbersome and off most the time. I feel like I'm moving freely in a world where I should be moving tile by tile. It's too easy to just sliiightly move onto a spike tile while trying to line up your dash when there's no room for error. PROS: Nice little game for the price however. Wouldn't be my first choice to start into these types of games but if you already know you like similar games then this isn't bad. Good if you need something to do while waiting.

review_title: Adaptive Slayer Here With His Honest Review
review_text: This game is like Legend of Zelda for those who like masterpiece retro games. Here is my review so far: Pros: 1. Simple controls that are easy to learn. 2. Teleport stones for fast travel (symbol on lower right map tiles once found). 3. Crafting is easy with Recipes that can let you craft more goodies. 4. Fun as well as challenging puzzles. 5. Interesting storyline. 6. Variety of NPCs with some appearing only at Day or Night. 7. Save points are beds you sleep in to choose Day or Night to wake up. 8. Upgrades for equipment. Cons: 1. Grinding to unlock all upgrades can be tedious. 2. Dying resets all progress to the last time you saved sleeping in a bed. 3. Heroic difficulty locked until game is finished on Normal (I only say this because I like playing games on the hardest difficulties and if I wanted "Tutorial" games I would be on PS4). Overall Rating: 5/5

review_text: Game is very good and enjoyable, adds so much new stuff and the game feels like it had alot of love and care put into it. The game feels amazing to play, the music, the art, and the all the new features added make River City Girls 2 a great experience. And I gotta hand it to WayForward, even though most of the locations are somewhat the same compared to the original RCG with a few new ones added, they still made River City look fabulous. Additionally, I really like that they added some online play to the game because that was one of the things that the original game needed and that made it really convenient for people who can't really find other friends around to play the game with. Overall, I'm very pleased with what I recieved with RCG2 and would recommend this game to anyone looking for a new game to play or any og fans who want some more River City Action! Doctor Cat is, at its heart, a jigsaw puzzle game. There are 12 images, with square pieces instead of cut shapes already set on the board. You swap pairs anywhere, not just next to one another. Difficulty determines how many square pieces are used. Wrapped around each puzzle is a small story -a patient kitty who has an issue, a high level description of their issue, the picture matching the theme (bill stress, unhealthy eating, gambling, etc.), and then the Doc saying a short platitude about working together to fix the issue. The game's issues, however, need analysis. In the Office, you can change the difficulty. Scrolling the text interacts with them by default. Also, you are stuck in the office; you need to start a puzzle for Menu to work. The menu is also confusing. Hard mode is hidden in the gallery, but Easy mode isn't. The painful part is the puzzle UI. PC/mouse may be good, but Xbox controller gave me RSI. No quick moves, except from just the left/right border.

review_text: Overalll, it's a more complex stardew. It's hard to get into due to the controlls not being customizable. There's no back button, your tools are designated to the D-pad and if i have an item in slot 5 that i want to use after D-pad the only way back to slot 5 is tapping RB 5 times. After doing this a couple times in a row, it gets tedious. The player character is scripted, games like these are better off with a strong silent type character who has minimal dialogue but, but in this game they get full paragraphs with minimal player input, so it's a lot of your character talking. The pet companion needs spacing, you start off with a talking cat that constantly hovers over your character that blocks interaction, which is problem when farming. The map in this game is very vague, each region image looks the surface of mars but blurry, no indication on what is there only a short name.

review_text: Im enjoyinging playing this game very much. The art style is not my normal thing but ive found my self enjoying it very much in spite of that small detail. The game loop is pretty simple but seems to be expanding as the game progresses which i am enjoying. There are a few tweeks that could be made including the areas of the map where the character's movement seems to be blocked or slowed by invisible objects and a Qol improvement to have tool tips to appear when navigating shop inventory would be great. That way we would know better what we are buying before spending our hard earned currency on an item we dont really need yet. Controlls could be refined, perhaps allow a deadzone to be defined by players on controllers to prevent snap back that spins the directional orientation of the character away for the intended target when the player releases the annolog stick during farming tasks. Still mostly great so far and i cant wait to see how the devs improve from here.

Most of the mazes are singular paths with no puzzle solving really required. I think if the pacing was changed so that the content of level 31+ was introduced around level 11 and we got more mazes that played like the last 5 levels this would be perfect. With all that said, the last 20 levels are good enough to be worth getting through the first 30 and a 5 star review.

First is aiming this game had fog originally draw distance is higher but distance can affect shots at times. The other is head bobbing turn it off aiming is better. To me there just isn't enough random encounters and it feels like I'm doing the same thing over and over again with little variation. Plus the game has a big problem with boss variety. There's only 5 major bosses in total,that's pretty small compared to other rougelikes like dead cells or hades. The game is genuinely good and I'm having fun but having more bosses and some more unique zones with crazier Rng would make the game immensly better.

review_title: Wow, okay.. this game is actually rather good!
review_text: What a surprise! I almost overlooked this title, and one could easily shrug it off after seeing the letters 'FMV'. However the execution here can be called perfect! Sharp HD visuals with excellent production values makes you feel like you're watching a recent modern film release. But the real draw here is the authentic Choose Your Own Adventure style gameplay which makes this both refreshingly casual, yet remarkably exciting! Its a gem that sufficiently scratches a major itch you never even knew you had! It's not perfect, as the video seems to pause on rare occasion, consequently having to briefly accelerate just to catch up (in my experiences). The only other quibble is that being a British game, some non-native players may have trouble following the heavily accented dialogue. There are subtitles, but they take something away from the overall cinematic presentation, in my opinion. Otherwise, the game is a very nice diversion, especially if you're looking for something somewhat unique!

review_title: Group rogueish boardgame, not a pure strategy boardgame
review_text: I played this back when it was on GP and I thought it was okay for the strategy boardgame genre. I was not impressed. I gave it another try. My original assessment was right. It's much better as a group rogue style game and played that way. You are NOT going to win. It's not a strategy rpg board game. Your goal should be to grind out books BEFORE you lose. Books are used to unlock classes, better gear, and POSITIVE events. Use everything you have to finish a dungeon or kill a chaos boss to get lore books. Tips Focus on books! Ignore the chaos meter. At lvl 3 towers will pop that you destroy to lower to 2. Make sure you have 1 toon with high STR, SPD, and INT to destroy towers. Do "easy" town quests. Make sure you have 1+ high physical DAM and 1+ magic DAM to bypass resists. Avoid Herbalist. Heal skill only works when using an herb. Prices escalate quickly. You NEED all money for gear, not herbs. Tinder pouch(camp) is your heal. Lasts many turns, just go back.

the graphics and puzzles are amazing. The story line is not very clear and the ending definitely felt unfinished. It doesn't explain what was going on in the end. If she was actually in a hospital. It doesn't explain any of her struggles. IMO they left way to much up for interpretation and failed to give any clear answers. It was a fun play through though. The game graphics are amazing and it does a good job of making you want to play more to understand what's happening and the puzzles are really challenging. Only taking a star off because of the lack of answers in the end.

Dialog is alot of padding and repeated to fill gaps between puzzles. My guess is this was written or translated by someone with English as their second language. The puzzles are great and the game doesn't overstay. Could maybe have been 30 mins shorter or so, but overall it was a fun game.

The game is a lot of puzzles involving shadows, and how to make them bigger and smaller or change shape. Unfortunately most of its mind-bending tricks were already done in other games (like driving a train towards the light to make the shadow bigger) and so a lot of the puzzles were pretty easy to solve. The collectables are supposed to be a optional challenge but in truth they are the only place you will ever feel a challenge, and barely at that. There is a deeper story here about a girl who has paranoid schizophrenia but I wasn't really interested enough to see it to its conclusion. I'm sure people who can relate will have more connection.

I played through this on the Xbox Ally handheld before it left Game Pass. It took me about 7 hours to complete the story and get the majority of the collectibles. At first I really enjoyed my time with the game. The art style and gameplay mechanics were unique and fun! The puzzles were interesting. Eventually I got tired of the game though, and just wanted it to be over. I used a guide to help me through some of the parts I got stuck in during the last third of the game. I'm glad I tried it out. If you like artsy puzzle games, it's definitely worth checking out! Not exactly for me, however.

If you like puzzle-platforms like Gris and Limbo, essentially games that have a terrific artstyle and an understated story then this is the game for you. review_text: 4 stars bc the game is exactly what youd expect. Non linear, simple walking sim through liminal space. The VHS aesthetic layered over clean graphics works well. The sound design is good, use headphones. That being said, if you are like me and have never understood the hype around liminal spaces, this game wont help you understand. This is considered a psych horror game, and not once did I feel anything other than boredom. Not trapped, or claustrophobic, or anxious. Just felt like I was wasting my time. I was hoping the immersion in a game like this would help me 'get it,' and I guess this has proved Im just not the target audience for this sort of thing. Im only saying all this to make it clear that this is not a game for everyone, but if you really enjoy the aesthetics of liminal spaces this game does it well.

review_text: I am a big fan of this subgenre of games; however, the opening hours of many games in the subgenre leave players stuck in the mire of bad maps, gated mechanics, & general drudgery. Ender Magnolias is the exception. The player starts with many movement & combat mechanic, but the true star of the show is the map: differentiating between unmapped, mapped but unexplored, and fully mapped is discernable at a glance. If that weren't enough, as you acquire mechanics, the previously locked areas gates on the map show a different color, AND show the applicable mechanic to open the area! Most metroidvanias get in their own (and the player's) wayof the "fun". Not Ender Magnolias. This has been my first ever game review, written with controller. Support these good people. -K

Thats because you control each foot with your stick and flick them like real skating. This game really gives you the feel of actually skateboarding and honestly for me it has the best feel I've ever experienced. You can make tricks look so clean and realistic. It's not an easy game but thats what makes it so fun. It gives it a long life span. Keep in mind you can make the game easier because there's a ton of settings. And it manages a great, authentic SW feel that gets me right in the "'member? berries" w/o squeezing too hard. Idunno, maybe if I played the game at launch, I would've been a lot harsher, but as it is, I am enjoying myself quite a bit. It's the game I keep coming back to. It's the game I keep missing when I'm doing something else. I didn't expect that. Not from Ubisoft. Does it have issues? Sure, but who cares? It still manages to fulfill my lifelong wish of being a scoundrel in the SW universe since the 70s, and it does it pretty well.

review_text: Post update update: Significantly better now. Do developers even test their own games anymore? I wanted to like this game so badly, but the sheer volume of stealth in this game is absolutely exhausting. Every failed attempt results in a reloaded save from 30 minutes ago. Loads of lost progress. Heaven forfend you were on the other side of the map, now you have to drive for 5mins just to get back to where you were. The cherry on top is that the stealth is abysmal. From a studio that has given us some magnificent stealth games, this one plays like a 2000 splinter cell entry. The only marks Ican give this game is: Nix is cute, Sabacc is fun, and as always, Ubi knows how to immerse you in a world and make it feel alive. If the actual gameplay of this game was broader and better executed, this game could have been an 8/10. Being almost exclusively a stealth game, and not a particularly good one at that, it gets a 3/10 from me. Super disappointed in the direction they chose to take this game, given how long we've waited for more SW content and how few and far between they appear.
